ant_laudes.eng: You who left all * and follow me, you will receive hundredfolds, and you will have eternal life.
ant_laudes.lat: Vos qui reliquístis * ómnia, et secúti estis me, céntuplum accipiétis, et vitam ætérnam possidébitis.

ant_vespera.eng: For they shall deliver you * up to councils: and in the synagogues you shall be beaten: and you shall stand before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony unto them.
ant_vespera.lat: Tradent enim vos * in concíliis, et in synagógis suis flagellábunt vos, et ante reges et prǽsides ducémini propter me in testimónium illis, et Géntibus.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
Brothers: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Fratres: Jam non estis hóspites et ádvenæ: sed estis cives Sanctórum et doméstici Dei: superædificáti super fundaméntum Apostolórum, et Prophetárum, ipso summo angulári lápide Christo Jesu.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
V. And the Apostles indeed went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Ibant Apóstoli gaudéntes a conspéctu concílii, quóniam digni hábiti sunt pro nómine Jesu contuméliam pati.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Per manus autem Apostolórum fiébant signa et prodígia multa in plebe.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Now let the earth with joy resound,
And heaven the chant re-echo round;
Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise
The great Apostles' glorious praise.
O ye who, throned in glory dread,
Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.
Ye close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.
Sickness and health your voice obey;
At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.
So when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.
* Praise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Exsúltet orbis gáudiis:
Cælum resúltet láudibus:
Apostolórum glóriam
Tellus et astra cóncinunt.
Vos sæculórum júdices,
Et vera mundi lúmina:
Votis precámur córdium,
Audíte voces súpplicum.
Qui templa cæli cláuditis,
Serásque verbo sólvitis,
Nos a reátu nóxios
Solvi jubéte, quǽsumus.
Præcépta quorum prótinus
Languor salúsque séntiunt:
Sanáte mentes lánguidas:
Augéte nos virtútibus.
Ut, cum redíbit árbiter
In fine Christus sǽculi,
Nos sempitérni gáudii
Concédat esse cómpotes.
* Patri, simúlque Fílio,
Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
Sicut fuit, sit júgiter
Sæclum per omne glória.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Th' eternal gifts of Christ the King,
The Apostles' glory, let us sing;
And all with hearts of gladness raise
Due hymns of thankful love and praise.
For they the Church's princes are,
Triumphant leaders in the war,
The heavenly King's own warrior band,
True lights to lighten every land.
Theirs was the steadfast faith of saints,
The hope that never yields nor faints,
The love of Christ in perfect glow,
That lay the prince of this world low.
In them the Father's glory shone,
In them the Spirit's will was done,
The Son himself exults in them;
Joy fills the new Jerusalem.
* Praise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Ætérna Christi múnera,
Apostolórum glóriam,
Palmas et hymnos débitos
Lætis canámus méntibus.
Ecclesiárum Príncipes,
Belli triumpháles duces,
Cæléstis aulæ mílites,
Et vera mundi lúmina.
Devóta Sanctórum fides,
Invícta spes credéntium,
Perfécta Christi cáritas
Mundi tyránnum cónterit.
In his Patérna glória,
In his triúmphat Fílius,
In his volúntas Spíritus,
Cælum replétur gáudio.
* Patri, simúlque Fílio,
Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
Sicut fuit, sit júgiter
Sæclum per omne glória.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Hoc est præcéptum meum, * ut diligátis ínvicem, sicut diléxi vos.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Greater love than this no man hath, * that a man lay down his life for his friends.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Majórem caritátem * nemo habet, ut ánimam suam ponat quis pro amícis suis.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Vos amíci mei estis, * si fecéritis quæ præcípio vobis, dicit Dóminus.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Blessed are the peacemakers * the clean of heart, they shall see God.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Beáti pacífici, * beáti mundo corde: quóniam ipsi Deum vidébunt.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: In your patience * you shall possess your souls.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: In patiéntia vestra * possidébitis ánimas vestras.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: In omnem terram * exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
ant_1.eng: Their sound * hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.
ant_2.eng: The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.eng: The horns of the just * shall be exalted. Alleluia.

nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Nimis honoráti sunt amíci tui, Deus.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. Thy friends, O Lord, are made exceedingly honourable.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: In omnem terram * exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Their sound * hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Clamavérunt justi, * et Dóminus exaudívit eos.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The just cried * and the Lord heard them.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Constítues eos * príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thou shalt make them princes * over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Dedísti hereditátem * timéntibus nomen tuum, Dómine.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Thou hast given an inheritance * to them that fear thy name, O Lord.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Annuntiavérunt * ópera Dei, et facta ejus intellexérunt.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: They declared * the works of God, and understood his doings.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: The horns of the just * shall be exalted. Alleluia.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Lux orta est * justo, allelúja, rectis corde lætítia, allelúja.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: Light is risen * to the just, alleluia, and joy to the right of heart. Alleluia.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Custodiébant * testimónia ejus, et præcépta ejus, allelúja.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: They kept his testimonies, * and the commandment which he gave them. Alleluia.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 18

verses.lat: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum ejus annúntiat firmaméntum.
verses.eng: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

verses.lat: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
verses.eng: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

verses.lat: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
verses.eng: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

verses.lat: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
verses.eng: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

verses.lat: 18:6a In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
verses.eng: 18:6a He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

verses.lat: 18:6b Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * (7a) a summo cælo egréssio ejus:
verses.eng: 18:6b Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * (7a) his going out is from the end of heaven,

verses.lat: 18:7b Et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre ejus.
verses.eng: 18:7b And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

verses.lat: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
verses.eng: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

verses.lat: 18:9 Justítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
verses.eng: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

verses.lat: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * judícia Dómini vera, justificáta in semetípsa.
verses.eng: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

verses.lat: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
verses.eng: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

verses.lat: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
verses.eng: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

verses.lat: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? † ab occúltis meis munda me: * (14a) et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
verses.eng: 18:13 Who can understand sins? † from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * (14a) and from those of others spare thy servant.

verses.lat: 18:14b Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
verses.eng: 18:14b If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

verses.lat: 18:15a Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
verses.eng: 18:15a And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

verses.lat: 18:15b Dómine, adjútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
verses.eng: 18:15b O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: In omnem terram * exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Their sound * hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 33

verses.lat: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus ejus in ore meo.
verses.eng: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

verses.lat: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
verses.eng: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

verses.lat: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
verses.eng: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

verses.lat: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
verses.eng: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

verses.lat: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
verses.eng: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

verses.lat: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus ejus salvávit eum.
verses.eng: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

verses.lat: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
verses.eng: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
verses.eng: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

verses.lat: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
verses.eng: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

verses.lat: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
verses.eng: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

verses.lat: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
verses.eng: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

verses.lat: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
verses.eng: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

verses.lat: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
verses.eng: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

verses.lat: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
verses.eng: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

verses.lat: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super justos: * et aures ejus in preces eórum.
verses.eng: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

verses.lat: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
verses.eng: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

verses.lat: 33:18 Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
verses.eng: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

verses.lat: 33:19 Juxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
verses.eng: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

verses.lat: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes justórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
verses.eng: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
verses.eng: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

verses.lat: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt justum, delínquent.
verses.eng: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

verses.lat: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
verses.eng: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Clamavérunt justi, * et Dóminus exaudívit eos.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: The just cried * and the Lord heard them.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 44

verses.lat: 44:2a Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
verses.eng: 44:2a My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

verses.lat: 44:2b Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
verses.eng: 44:2b My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

verses.lat: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, † diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: † grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

verses.lat: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
verses.eng: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

verses.lat: 44:5a Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
verses.eng: 44:5a With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

verses.lat: 44:5b Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 44:5b Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

verses.lat: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

verses.lat: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
verses.eng: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

verses.lat: 44:8 Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
verses.eng: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

verses.lat: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te (10a) fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
verses.eng: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which (10a) the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

verses.lat: 44:10b Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
verses.eng: 44:10b The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

verses.lat: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
verses.eng: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

verses.lat: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
verses.eng: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

verses.lat: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
verses.eng: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

verses.lat: 44:14 Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis (15a) circumamícta varietátibus.
verses.eng: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, (15a) clothed round about with varieties.

verses.lat: 44:15b Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
verses.eng: 44:15b After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

verses.lat: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

verses.lat: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
verses.eng: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

verses.lat: 44:18a Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 44:18a They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

verses.lat: 44:18b Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 44:18b Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Constítues eos * príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Thou shalt make them princes * over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 46

verses.lat: 46:2 Omnes gentes, pláudite mánibus: * jubiláte Deo in voce exsultatiónis.
verses.eng: 46:2 O clap your hands, all ye nations: * shout unto God with the voice of joy,

verses.lat: 46:3 Quóniam Dóminus excélsus, terríbilis: * Rex magnus super omnem terram.
verses.eng: 46:3 For the Lord is high, terrible: * a great king over all the earth.

verses.lat: 46:4 Subjécit pópulos nobis: * et gentes sub pédibus nostris.
verses.eng: 46:4 He hath subdued the people under us; * and the nations under our feet.

verses.lat: 46:5 Elégit nobis hereditátem suam: * spéciem Jacob, quam diléxit.
verses.eng: 46:5 He hath chosen for us his inheritance, * the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.

verses.lat: 46:6 Ascéndit Deus in júbilo: * et Dóminus in voce tubæ.
verses.eng: 46:6 God is ascended with jubilee, * and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.

verses.lat: 46:7 Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
verses.eng: 46:7 Sing praises to our God, sing ye: * sing praises to our king, sing ye.

verses.lat: 46:8 Quóniam Rex omnis terræ Deus: * psállite sapiénter.
verses.eng: 46:8 For God is the king of all the earth: * sing ye wisely.

verses.lat: 46:9 Regnábit Deus super gentes: * Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
verses.eng: 46:9 God shall reign over the nations: * God sitteth on his holy throne.

verses.lat: 46:10 Príncipes populórum congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham: * quóniam dii fortes terræ veheménter eleváti sunt.
verses.eng: 46:10 The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: * for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 60

verses.lat: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
verses.eng: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

verses.lat: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
verses.eng: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

verses.lat: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
verses.eng: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.

verses.lat: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
verses.eng: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

verses.lat: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

verses.lat: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos ejus usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
verses.eng: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

verses.lat: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem ejus quis requíret?
verses.eng: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

verses.lat: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
verses.eng: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Dedísti hereditátem * timéntibus nomen tuum, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: Thou hast given an inheritance * to them that fear thy name, O Lord.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 63

verses.lat: 63:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam cum déprecor: * a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 63:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee: * deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.

verses.lat: 63:3 Protexísti me a convéntu malignántium: * a multitúdine operántium iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 63:3 Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; * from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.

verses.lat: 63:4 Quia exacuérunt ut gládium linguas suas: * intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum.
verses.eng: 63:4 For they have whetted their tongues like a sword; * they have bent their bow a bitter thing, to shoot in secret the undefiled.

verses.lat: 63:6 Súbito sagittábunt eum, et non timébunt: * firmavérunt sibi sermónem nequam.
verses.eng: 63:6 They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: * they are resolute in wickedness.

verses.lat: 63:6 Narravérunt ut abscónderent láqueos: * dixérunt: Quis vidébit eos?
verses.eng: 63:6 They have talked of hiding snares; * they have said: Who shall see them?

verses.lat: 63:7 Scrutáti sunt iniquitátes: * defecérunt scrutántes scrutínio.
verses.eng: 63:7 They have searched after iniquities: * they have failed in their search.

verses.lat: 63:7 Accédet homo ad cor altum: * et exaltábitur Deus.
verses.eng: 63:7 Man shall come to a deep heart: * and God shall be exalted.

verses.lat: 63:8 Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum: * et infirmátæ sunt contra eos linguæ eórum.
verses.eng: 63:8 The arrows of children are their wounds: * and their tongues against them are made weak.

verses.lat: 63:9 Conturbáti sunt omnes qui vidébant eos: * et tímuit omnis homo.
verses.eng: 63:9 All that saw them were troubled; * and every man was afraid.

verses.lat: 63:10 Et annuntiavérunt ópera Dei, * et facta ejus intellexérunt.
verses.eng: 63:10 And they declared the works of God: * and understood his doings.

verses.lat: 63:11 Lætábitur justus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo, * et laudabúntur omnes recti corde.
verses.eng: 63:11 The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him: * and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Annuntiavérunt * ópera Dei, et facta ejus intellexérunt.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: They declared * the works of God, and understood his doings.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 74

verses.lat: 74:2 Confitébimur tibi, Deus: * confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
verses.eng: 74:2 We will praise thee, O God: * we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.

verses.lat: 74:3 Narrábimus mirabília tua: * cum accépero tempus, ego justítias judicábo.
verses.eng: 74:3 We will relate thy wondrous works: * when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.

verses.lat: 74:4 Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: * ego confirmávi colúmnas ejus.
verses.eng: 74:4 The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: * I have established the pillars thereof.

verses.lat: 74:5 Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: * et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
verses.eng: 74:5 I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: * and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.

verses.lat: 74:6 Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: * nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 74:6 Lift not up your horn on high: * speak not iniquity against God.

verses.lat: 74:7 Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: * quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: 74:7 For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: * for God is the judge.

verses.lat: 74:8 Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: * quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
verses.eng: 74:8 One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: * for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.

verses.lat: 74:9 Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx ejus non est exinaníta: * bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
verses.eng: 74:9 And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: * all the sinners of the earth shall drink.

verses.lat: 74:10 Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: * cantábo Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 74:10 But I will declare for ever: * I will sing to the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 74:11 Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: * et exaltabúntur córnua justi.
verses.eng: 74:11 And I will break all the horns of sinners: * but the horns of the just shall be exalted.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: The horns of the just * shall be exalted. Alleluia.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 96

verses.lat: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
verses.eng: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

verses.lat: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu ejus: * justítia, et judícium corréctio sedis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

verses.lat: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos ejus.
verses.eng: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

verses.lat: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
verses.eng: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

verses.lat: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
verses.eng: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

verses.lat: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli justítiam ejus: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam ejus.
verses.eng: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

verses.lat: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
verses.eng: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

verses.lat: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
verses.eng: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

verses.lat: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Judæ, * propter judícia tua, Dómine:
verses.eng: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

verses.lat: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
verses.eng: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

verses.lat: 96:11 Lux orta est justo, * et rectis corde lætítia.
verses.eng: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

verses.lat: 96:12 Lætámini, justi, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Lux orta est * justo, allelúja, rectis corde lætítia, allelúja.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: Light is risen * to the just, alleluia, and joy to the right of heart. Alleluia.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 98

verses.lat: 98:1 Dóminus regnávit, irascántur pópuli: * qui sedet super Chérubim, moveátur terra.
verses.eng: 98:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry: * he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved.

verses.lat: 98:2 Dóminus in Sion magnus: * et excélsus super omnes pópulos.
verses.eng: 98:2 The Lord is great in Sion, * and high above all people.

verses.lat: 98:3 Confiteántur nómini tuo magno: quóniam terríbile, et sanctum est: * et honor regis judícium díligit.
verses.eng: 98:3 Let them give praise to thy great name: for it is terrible and holy: * and the king’s honour loveth judgment.

verses.lat: 98:4 Tu parásti directiónes: * judícium et justítiam in Jacob tu fecísti.
verses.eng: 98:4 Thou hast prepared directions: * thou hast done judgment and justice in Jacob.

verses.lat: 98:5 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte scabéllum pedum ejus: * quóniam sanctum est.
verses.eng: 98:5 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore his footstool, * for it is holy.

verses.lat: 98:6 Móyses et Aaron in sacerdótibus ejus: * et Sámuel inter eos, qui ínvocant nomen ejus:
verses.eng: 98:6 Moses and Aaron among his priests: * and Samuel among them that call upon his name.

verses.lat: 98:6 Invocábant Dóminum, et ipse exaudiébat eos: * in colúmna nubis loquebátur ad eos.
verses.eng: 98:6 They called upon the Lord, and he heard them: * he spoke to them in the pillar of the cloud.

verses.lat: 98:7 Custodiébant testimónia ejus, * et præcéptum quod dedit illis.
verses.eng: 98:7 They kept his testimonies, * and the commandment which he gave them.

verses.lat: 98:8 Dómine, Deus noster, tu exaudiébas eos: * Deus, tu propítius fuísti eis, et ulcíscens in omnes adinventiónes eórum.
verses.eng: 98:8 Thou didst hear them, O Lord our God: * thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions.

verses.lat: 98:9 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte in monte sancto ejus: * quóniam sanctus Dóminus, Deus noster.
verses.eng: 98:9 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore at his holy mountain: * for the Lord our God is holy.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Custodiébant * testimónia ejus, et præcépta ejus, allelúja.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: They kept his testimonies, * and the commandment which he gave them. Alleluia.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: In omnem terram * exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: Their sound * hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.eng: The horns of the just * shall be exalted. Alleluia.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 109

verses.lat: 109:1a Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
verses.eng: 109:1a The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

verses.lat: 109:1b Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:1b Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

verses.lat: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

verses.lat: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
verses.eng: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

verses.lat: 109:4 Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
verses.eng: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

verses.lat: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
verses.eng: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

verses.lat: 109:6 Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
verses.eng: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

verses.lat: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
verses.eng: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Jurávit Dóminus, * et non pœnitébit eum: Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: The Lord hath sworn * and will not repent: thou art a Priest for ever.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 112

verses.lat: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

verses.lat: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória ejus.
verses.eng: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

verses.lat: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * (6) et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
verses.eng: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * (6) and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

verses.lat: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
verses.eng: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

verses.lat: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
verses.eng: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

verses.lat: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
verses.eng: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Cóllocet eum * Dóminus cum princípibus pópuli sui.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: That the Lord may set him * with the princes of his people.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 115

verses.lat: 115:1 Crédidi, propter quod locútus sum: * ego autem humiliátus sum nimis.
verses.eng: 115:1 I have believed, therefore have I spoken; * but I have been humbled exceedingly.

verses.lat: 115:2 Ego dixi in excéssu meo: * Omnis homo mendax.
verses.eng: 115:2 I said in my excess: * Every man is a liar.

verses.lat: 115:3 Quid retríbuam Dómino, * pro ómnibus, quæ retríbuit mihi?
verses.eng: 115:3 What shall I render to the Lord, * for all the things that he hath rendered to me?

verses.lat: 115:4 Cálicem salutáris accípiam: * et nomen Dómini invocábo.
verses.eng: 115:4 I will take the chalice of salvation; * and I will call upon the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 115:5 Vota mea Dómino reddam coram omni pópulo ejus: * (6) pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini mors sanctórum ejus:
verses.eng: 115:5 I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people: * (6) precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

verses.lat: 115:7a O Dómine, quia ego servus tuus: * ego servus tuus, et fílius ancíllæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 115:7a O Lord, for I am thy servant: * I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid.

verses.lat: 115:7b Dirupísti víncula mea: ‡ (8) tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, * et nomen Dómini invocábo.
verses.eng: 115:7b Thou hast broken my bonds: ‡ (8) I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise, * and I will call upon the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 115:9 Vota mea Dómino reddam in conspéctu omnis pópuli ejus: * (10) in átriis domus Dómini, in médio tui, Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 115:9 I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people: * (10) in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Dirupísti, Dómine, * víncula mea: tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: O Lord, thou hast loosed my bonds; * I will offer thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 125

verses.lat: 125:1 In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion: * facti sumus sicut consoláti:
verses.eng: 125:1 When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, * we became like men comforted.

verses.lat: 125:2a Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: * et lingua nostra exsultatióne.
verses.eng: 125:2a Then was our mouth filled with gladness; * and our tongue with joy.

verses.lat: 125:2b Tunc dicent inter gentes: * Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.
verses.eng: 125:2b Then shall they say among the Gentiles: * The Lord hath done great things for them.

verses.lat: 125:3 Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobíscum: * facti sumus lætántes.
verses.eng: 125:3 The Lord hath done great things for us: * we are become joyful.

verses.lat: 125:4 Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, * sicut torrens in Austro.
verses.eng: 125:4 Turn again our captivity, O Lord, * as a stream in the south.

verses.lat: 125:5 Qui séminant in lácrimis, * in exsultatióne metent.
verses.eng: 125:5 They that sow in tears * shall reap in joy.

verses.lat: 125:6a Eúntes ibant et flebant, * mitténtes sémina sua.
verses.eng: 125:6a Going they went and wept, * casting their seeds.

verses.lat: 125:6b Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, * portántes manípulos suos.
verses.eng: 125:6b But coming they shall come with joyfulness, * carrying their sheaves.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Eúntes ibant * et flebant, mitténtes sémina sua.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: They went forth weeping * sowing their seed.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 138

verses.lat: 138:1 Dómine, probásti me, et cognovísti me: * (2) tu cognovísti sessiónem meam, et resurrectiónem meam.
verses.eng: 138:1 Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me: * (2) thou hast known my sitting down, and my rising up.

verses.lat: 138:3 Intellexísti cogitatiónes meas de longe: * sémitam meam, et funículum meum investigásti.
verses.eng: 138:3 Thou hast understood my thoughts afar off: * my path and my life thou hast searched out.

verses.lat: 138:4 Et omnes vias meas prævidísti: * quia non est sermo in lingua mea.
verses.eng: 138:4 And thou hast foreseen all my ways: * for there is no speech on my tongue.

verses.lat: 138:5 Ecce, Dómine, tu cognovísti ómnia novíssima, et antíqua: * tu formásti me, et posuísti super me manum tuam.
verses.eng: 138:5 Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last and those of old: * thou hast formed me, and hast laid thy hand upon me.

verses.lat: 138:6 Mirábilis facta est sciéntia tua ex me: * confortáta est, et non pótero ad eam.
verses.eng: 138:6 Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me: * it is high, and I cannot reach to it.

verses.lat: 138:7 Quo ibo a spíritu tuo? * et quo a fácie tua fúgiam?
verses.eng: 138:7 Whither shall I go from thy spirit? * or whither shall I flee from thy face?

verses.lat: 138:8 Si ascéndero in cælum, tu illic es: * si descéndero in inférnum, ades.
verses.eng: 138:8 If I ascend into heaven, thou art there: * if I descend into hell, thou art present.

verses.lat: 138:9 Si súmpsero pennas meas dilúculo, * et habitávero in extrémis maris:
verses.eng: 138:9 If I take my wings early in the morning, * and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea:

verses.lat: 138:10 Étenim illuc manus tua dedúcet me: * et tenébit me déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 138:10 Even there also shall thy hand lead me: * and thy right hand shall hold me.

verses.lat: 138:11 Et dixi: Fórsitan ténebræ conculcábunt me: * et nox illuminátio mea in delíciis meis.
verses.eng: 138:11 And I said: Perhaps darkness shall cover me: * and night shall be my light in my pleasures.

verses.lat: 138:12 Quia ténebræ non obscurabúntur a te, † et nox sicut dies illuminábitur: * sicut ténebræ ejus, ita et lumen ejus.
verses.eng: 138:12 But darkness shall not be dark to thee, † and night shall be light as the day: * the darkness thereof, and the light thereof are alike to thee.

verses.lat: 138:13 Quia tu possedísti renes meos: * suscepísti me de útero matris meæ.
verses.eng: 138:13 For thou hast possessed my reins: * thou hast protected me from my mother’s womb.

verses.lat: 138:14 Confitébor tibi quia terribíliter magnificátus es: ‡ mirabília ópera tua, * et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
verses.eng: 138:14 I will praise thee, for thou art fearfully magnified: ‡ wonderful are thy works, * and my soul knoweth right well.

verses.lat: 138:15 Non est occultátum os meum a te, quod fecísti in occúlto: * et substántia mea in inferióribus terræ.
verses.eng: 138:15 My bone is not hidden from thee, which thou hast made in secret: * and my substance in the lower parts of the earth.

verses.lat: 138:16 Imperféctum meum vidérunt óculi tui, † et in libro tuo omnes scribéntur: * dies formabúntur, et nemo in eis.
verses.eng: 138:16 Thy eyes did see my imperfect being, † and in thy book all shall be written: * days shall be formed, and no one in them.

verses.lat: 138:17 Mihi autem nimis honorificáti sunt amíci tui, Deus: * nimis confortátus est principátus eórum.
verses.eng: 138:17 But to me thy friends, O God, are made exceedingly honourable: * their principality is exceedingly strengthened.

verses.lat: 138:18 Dinumerábo eos, et super arénam multiplicabúntur: * exsurréxi, et adhuc sum tecum.
verses.eng: 138:18 I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand: * I rose up and am still with thee.

verses.lat: 138:19 Si occíderis, Deus, peccatóres: * viri sánguinum, declináte a me:
verses.eng: 138:19 If thou wilt kill the wicked, O God: * ye men of blood, depart from me:

verses.lat: 138:20 Quia dícitis in cogitatióne: * Accípient in vanitáte civitátes tuas.
verses.eng: 138:20 Because you say in thought: * They shall receive thy cities in vain.

verses.lat: 138:21 Nonne qui odérunt te, Dómine, óderam? * et super inimícos tuos tabescébam?
verses.eng: 138:21 Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hated thee: * and pined away because of thy enemies?

verses.lat: 138:22 Perfécto ódio óderam illos: * et inimíci facti sunt mihi.
verses.eng: 138:22 I have hated them with a perfect hatred: * and they are become enemies to me.

verses.lat: 138:23 Proba me, Deus, et scito cor meum: * intérroga me, et cognósce sémitas meas.
verses.eng: 138:23 Prove me, O God, and know my heart: * examine me, and know my paths.

verses.lat: 138:24 Et vide, si via iniquitátis in me est: * et deduc me in via ætérna.
verses.eng: 138:24 And see if there be in me the way of iniquity: * and lead me in the eternal way.

vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Confortátus est * principátus eórum, et honoráti sunt amíci tui, Deus.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: O God, thy friends are honourable; * their power is waxen right strong.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:
* Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
V. Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.
R. Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
responsory1.eng:
R. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord:
* Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.
V. Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light.
R. Be ye therefore wise as serpents and simple as doves.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Tóllite jugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:
* Jugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
V. Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.
R. Jugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
responsory2.eng:
R. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.
* For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.
V. And you shall find rest to your souls.
R. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:
* Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
V. Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.
R. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
&Gloria
R. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
responsory3.eng:
R. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak:
* for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:
V. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.
R. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.
&Gloria
R. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Vidi conjúnctos viros, habéntes spléndidas vestes, et Ángelus Dómini locútus est ad me, dicens:
* Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.
V. Vidi Ángelum Dei fortem, volántem per médium cælum, voce magna clamántem et dicéntem.
R. Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.
responsory4.eng:
R. I saw men standing together, clad in shining raiment, and the Angel of the Lord spoke unto me, saying:
* These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.
V. I saw a strong Angel of God fly into the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice:
R. These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Beáti estis, cum maledíxerint vobis hómines, et persecúti vos fúerint, et díxerint omne malum advérsum vos, mentiéntes, propter me:
* Gaudéte et exsultáte, quóniam merces vestra copiósa est in cælis.
V. Cum vos óderint hómines, et cum separáverint vos, et exprobráverint, et ejécerint nomen vestrum tamquam malum propter Fílium hóminis.
R. Gaudéte et exsultáte, quóniam merces vestra copiósa est in cælis.
responsory5.eng:
R. Blessed are ye when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for My sake;
* Rejoice, and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven.
V. When men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man's sake.
R. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Isti sunt triumphatóres et amíci Dei, qui contemnéntes jussa príncipum, meruérunt prǽmia ætérna:
* Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam.
V. Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.
R. Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam.
&Gloria
R. Modo coronántur, et accípiunt palmam.
responsory6.eng:
R. These are they which have conquered, and are become the friends of God, who recked not of the commandments of princes, and earned the everlasting reward.
* And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.
V. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
R. And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.
&Gloria
R. And now have they crowns on their heads, and palms in their hands.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Isti sunt qui vivéntes in carne, plantavérunt Ecclésiam sánguine suo:
* Cálicem Dómini bibérunt, et amíci Dei facti sunt.
V. In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
R. Cálicem Dómini bibérunt, et amíci Dei facti sunt.
responsory7.eng:
R. These are they who while yet they lived in the flesh, planted the Church in their own blood;
* They drank of the Lord's cup, and became the friends of God.
V. Their sound is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
R. They drank of the Lord's cup, and became the friends of God.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Isti sunt viri sancti, quos elégit Dóminus in caritáte non ficta, et dedit illis glóriam sempitérnam:
* Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.
V. Sancti per fidem vicérunt regna: operáti sunt justítiam.
R. Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.
&Gloria
R. Quorum doctrína fulget Ecclésia, ut sole luna.
responsory8.eng:
R. These men are saints, whom the Lord hath chosen in love unfeigned, and hath given them glory everlasting. These are they
* By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.
V. The saints through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness.
R. By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.
&Gloria
R. By the light of whose teaching the Church is glorified, even as the moon is glorified by the light of the sun.

ant_laudes.eng: O Blessed Mary, * Mother of God, Virgin for ever, temple of the Lord, sanctuary of the Holy Ghost, thou, without any example before thee, didst make thyself well-pleasing in the sight of our Lord Jesus Christ; pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God.
ant_laudes.lat: Beáta Dei Génetrix, María, * Virgo perpétua, templum Dómini, sacrárium Spíritus Sancti, sola sine exémplo placuísti Dómino nostro Jesu Christo: ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu.

ant_vespera.eng: Blessed Mother and inviolate Maiden! * Glorious Queen of the world! Plead for us with the Lord!
ant_vespera.lat: Beáta Mater * et intácta Virgo, gloriósa Regína mundi, intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum.

capitulum_laudes.eng: $Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Ab inítio et ante sǽcula creáta sum, et usque ad futúrum sǽculum non désinam, et in habitatióne sancta coram ipso ministrávi.
$Deo gratias.

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. As a plane tree by the water in the streets, I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon. and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
In platéis sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans odórem dedi: quasi myrrha elécta, dedi suavitátem odóris.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
v. And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem. And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Et sic in Sion firmáta sum, et in civitáte sanctificáta simíliter requiévi, et in Jerúsalem potéstas mea. Et radicávi in pópulo honorificáto, et in parte Dei mei heréditas illíus, et in plenitúdine sanctórum deténtio mea.
$Deo gratias.

hymnus_laudes.lat:
O gloriósa vírginum,
Sublímis inter sídera,
Qui te creávit, párvulum
Lacténte nutris úbere.
Quod Heva tristis ábstulit,
Tu reddis almo gérmine:
Intrent ut astra flébiles,
Cæli reclúdis cárdines.
Tu Regis alti jánua
Et aula lucis fúlgida:
Vitam datam per Vírginem,
Gentes redémptæ, pláudite.
* Jesu tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Quem terra, pontus, sídera
Colunt, adórant, prædicant,
Trinam regéntem máchinam,
Claustrum Maríæ bájulat.
Cui luna, sol, et ómnia
Desérviunt per témpora,
Perfúsa cæli grátia,
Gestant puéllæ víscera.
Beáta Mater múnere,
Cujus supérnus ártifex
Mundum pugíllo cóntinens,
Ventris sub arca clausus est.
Beáta cæli núntio,
Fœcúnda sancto Spíritu,
Desiderátus géntibus,
Cujus per alvum fusus est.
* Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
v. Ave, star of ocean,
Child divine who barest,
Mother, ever-Virgin,
Heaven's portal fairest.
Taking that sweet Ave
Erst by Gabriel spoken,
Eva's name reversing,
Be of peace the token.
Break the sinners' fetters,
Light to blind restoring,
All our ills dispelling,
Every boon imploring.
Show thyself a mother
In thy supplication;
He will hear who chose thee
At his incarnation.
Maid all maids excelling,
Passing meek and lowly,
Win for sinners pardon,
Make us chaste and holy.
As we onward journey
Aid our weak endeavour,
Till we gaze on Jesus
And rejoice forever.
Father, Son, and Spirit,
Three in One confessing,
Give we equal glory
Equal praise and blessing.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Ave maris stella,
Dei Mater alma,
Atque semper Virgo,
Felix cæli porta.
Sumens illud Ave
Gabriélis ore,
Funda nos in pace,
Mutans Hevæ nomen.
Solve vincla reis,
Profer lumen cæcis,
Mala nostra pelle,
Bona cuncta posce.
Monstra te esse matrem,
Sumat per te preces,
Qui pro nobis natus,
Tulit esse tuus.
Virgo singuláris,
Inter omnes mitis,
Nos culpis solútos
Mites fac et castos.
Vitam præsta puram,
Iter para tutum,
Ut vidéntes Jesum,
Semper collætémur.
Sit laus Deo Patri,
Summo Christo decus,
Spirítui Sancto,
Tribus honor unus.
Amen.

invit.eng: Hail Mary, full of grace, * The Lord is with thee.
invit.lat: Ave María, grátia plena, * Dóminus tecum.

lectio_prima.eng: v. As a plane tree by the water in the streets, I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon. and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh.
lectio_prima.lat: In platéis sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans odórem dedi: quasi myrrha elécta, dedi suavitátem odóris.

responsory_breve_nona.eng:
R.br. God hath chosen her, * and fore-chosen her.
V. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
R. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.
R. And fore-chosen her.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
V. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
R.br. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.
R. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.
V. In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.
R. Et præelégit eam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.

responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
R.br. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.
R. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.
V. Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
R. Deus vultu suo.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.

responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
R.br. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.
V. In thy comeliness and thy beauty.
R. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. In thy beauty.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
V. In thy comeliness and thy beauty.
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
R.br. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
R. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
V. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
R. Et pulchritúdine tua.

$Deo gratias.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
O glorious lady! throned on high
Above the star-illumined sky;
Thereto ordained, thy bosom lent
To thy Creator nourishment.
Through thy sweet offspring we receive
The bliss once lost through hapless Eve;
And heaven to mortals open lies
Now thou art portal of the skies.
Thou art the door of heaven's high King,
Light's gateway fair and glistering;
Life through a Virgin is restored;
Ye ransomed nations, praise the Lord!
All honour, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
O gloriósa vírginum,
Sublímis inter sídera,
Qui te creávit, párvulum
Lacténte nutris úbere.
Quod Heva tristis ábstulit,
Tu reddis almo gérmine:
Intrent ut astra flébiles,
Cæli reclúdis cárdines.
Tu Regis alti jánua
Et aula lucis fúlgida:
Vitam datam per Vírginem,
Gentes redémptæ, pláudite.
* Jesu tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
The God whom earth, and sea, and sky
Adore, and laud, and magnify,
Who o'er their threefold fabric reigns,
The Virgin's spotless womb contains.
The God, whose will by moon and sun
And all things in due course is done,
Is borne upon a maiden's breast,
By fullest heavenly grace possest.
How blest that mother, in whose shrine
The great artificer divine,
Whose hand contains the earth and sky,
Vouchsafed, as in his ark, to lie.
Blest, in the message Gabriel brought;
Blest, by the work the Spirit wrought;
From whom the great desire of earth
Took human flesh and human birth.
* All honour, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Quem terra, pontus, sídera
Colunt, adórant, prædicant,
Trinam regéntem máchinam,
Claustrum Maríæ bájulat.
Cui luna, sol, et ómnia
Desérviunt per témpora,
Perfúsa cæli grátia,
Gestant puéllæ víscera.
Beáta Mater múnere,
Cujus supérnus ártifex
Mundum pugíllo cóntinens,
Ventris sub arca clausus est.
Beáta cæli núntio,
Fœcúnda sancto Spíritu,
Desiderátus géntibus,
Cujus per alvum fusus est.
* Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Ave, star of ocean,
Child divine who barest,
Mother, ever-Virgin,
Heaven's portal fairest.
Taking that sweet Ave
Erst by Gabriel spoken,
Eva's name reversing,
Be of peace the token.
Break the sinners' fetters,
Light to blind restoring,
All our ills dispelling,
Every boon imploring.
Show thyself a mother
In thy supplication;
He will hear who chose thee
At his incarnation.
Maid all maids excelling,
Passing meek and lowly,
Win for sinners pardon,
Make us chaste and holy.
As we onward journey
Aid our weak endeavour,
Till we gaze on Jesus
And rejoice forever.
Father, Son, and Spirit,
Three in One confessing,
Give we equal glory
Equal praise and blessing.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Ave maris stella,
Dei Mater alma,
Atque semper Virgo,
Felix cæli porta.
Sumens illud Ave
Gabriélis ore,
Funda nos in pace,
Mutans Hevæ nomen.
Solve vincla reis,
Profer lumen cæcis,
Mala nostra pelle,
Bona cuncta posce.
Monstra te esse matrem,
Sumat per te preces,
Qui pro nobis natus,
Tulit esse tuus.
Virgo singuláris,
Inter omnes mitis,
Nos culpis solútos
Mites fac et castos.
Vitam præsta puram,
Iter para tutum,
Ut vidéntes Jesum,
Semper collætémur.
Sit laus Deo Patri,
Summo Christo decus,
Spirítui Sancto,
Tribus honor unus.
Amen.

invit.lat: Sancta María, Dei Génetrix Virgo, * Intercéde pro nobis.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O Holy Mother of God, thou art become beautiful * and gentle in thy gladness.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Speciósa * facta es et suávis in delíciis tuis, sancta Dei Génetrix.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Lo the winter is past, * the rain is over and gone. Rise up, my love, and come away.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Jam hiems tránsiit, * imber ábiit et recéssit: surge, amíca mea, et veni.

V. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.

Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.

responsory_breve_tertia.eng:

V. In thy comeliness and thy beauty.
R. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. In thy beauty.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Sancta et immaculáta virgínitas, quibus te láudibus éfferam, néscio: 
* Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulísti.
V. Benedícta tu in muliéribus, et benedíctus fructus ventris tui.
R. Quia quem cæli cápere non póterant, tuo grémio contulisti.
responsory1.eng:
R. O how holy and how spotless is thy virginity; I am too dull to praise thee:
* For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.
V. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
R. For thou hast borne in thy breast Him Whom the heavens cannot contain.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Congratulámini mihi, omnes qui dilígitis Dóminum: quia cum essem párvula, plácui Altíssimo, 
* Et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
V. Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
R. Et de meis viscéribus génui Deum et hóminem.
responsory2.eng:
R. Rejoice with me, all ye that love the Lord, for while I was yet a little one, I pleased the Most High.
* And I have brought forth from my bowels God and man.
V. All generations shall call me blessed, since the Lord hath regarded the lowliness of his handmaiden.
R. And I have brought forth from my bowels God and man.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Beáta es, Virgo María, quæ Dóminum portásti, Creatórem mundi: 
* Genuísti qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
V. Ave, María, grátia plena; Dóminus tecum.
R. Genuísti qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
&Gloria
R. Genuísti qui te fecit, et in ætérnum pérmanes Virgo.
responsory3.eng:
R. Blessed art thou, O Virgin Mary, who hast carried the Lord, the Maker of the world.
* Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.
V. Hail, Mary, full of grace. the Lord is with thee.
R. Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.
&Gloria
R. Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Sicut cedrus exaltáta sum in Líbano, et sicut cypréssus in monte Sion: quasi myrrha elécta, 
* Dedi suavitátem odóris.
V. Et sicut cinnamómum et bálsamum aromatízans.
R. Dedi suavitátem odóris.
responsory4.eng:
R. I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and as a cypress-tree upon Mount Zion. Like the best myrrh
* I yielded a pleasant odour.
V. Like cinnamon and sweet balsam.
R. I yielded a pleasant odour.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Quæ est ista quæ procéssit sicut sol, et formósa tamquam Jerúsalem? 
* Vidérunt eam fíliæ Sion, et beátam dixérunt, et regínæ laudavérunt eam.
V. Et sicut dies verni circúmdabant eam flores rosárum et lília convállium.
R. Vidérunt eam fíliæ Sion, et beátam dixérunt, et regínæ laudavérunt eam.
responsory5.eng:
R. Who is this that cometh up like the sun? This, comely as Jerusalem?
* The daughters of Zion saw her, and called her blessed: the queens also, and they praised her.
V. And about her it was as the flower of roses in the spring of the year, and lilies of the valleys.
R. The daughters of Zion saw her, and called her blessed the queens also, and they praised her.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Ornátam monílibus fíliam Jerúsalem Dóminus concupívit: 
* Et vidéntes eam fíliæ Sion, beatíssimam prædicavérunt, dicéntes: * Unguéntum effúsum nomen tuum.
V. Astitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.
R. Et vidéntes eam fíliæ Sion, beatíssimam prædicavérunt, dicéntes:
&Gloria
R. Unguéntum effúsum nomen tuum.
responsory6.eng:
R. When the Lord beheld the daughter of Jerusalem adorned with her jewels, He greatly desired her beauty
* And when the daughters of Zion saw her, they cried out that she was most blessed, saying thy name is as ointment poured forth.
V. Upon thy right hand did stand the Queen in a vesture of gold wrought about with diverse colours.
R. And when the daughters of Zion saw her, they cried out that she was most blessed, saying:
&Gloria
R. Thy name is as ointment poured forth.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Felix namque es, sacra Virgo María, et omni laude digníssima:
* Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus, Deus noster.
V. Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam festivitátem.
R. Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus, Deus noster.
responsory7.eng:
R. O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise
* For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.
V. Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God. May all that are keeping this thine holy Feast day feel the might of thine assistance.
R. For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes, 
* Quia fecit mihi Dóminus magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.
V. Et misericórdia ejus a progénie in progénies timéntibus eum.
R. Quia fecit mihi Dóminus magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.
&Gloria
R. Quia fecit mihi Dóminus magna qui potens est, et sanctum nomen ejus.
responsory8.eng:
R. All generations shall call me blessed.
* For He that is mighty, even the Lord, hath done to me great things; and Holy is His Name.
V. And his mercy is on them that fear Him, from generation to generation.
R. He that is mighty, even the Lord, hath done to me great things; and Holy is His Name.
&Gloria
R. He that is mighty, even the Lord, hath done to me great things; and Holy is His Name.

ant_laudes.eng: O Blessed Mary, * Mother of God, Virgin for ever, temple of the Lord, sanctuary of the Holy Ghost, thou, without any example before thee, didst make thyself well-pleasing in the sight of our Lord Jesus Christ; pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God.

R. Genuisti qui te fecit, et in æternum permanes Virgo.
responsory2.eng:
R. Blessed art thou, O Virgin Mary, who hast carried the Lord, the Maker of the world.
* Thou hast borne Him Who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.
V. Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
R. Thou hast borne him who created thee, and thou abidest a virgin for ever.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:

* Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus, Deus noster.
V. Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam commemoratiónem.
R. Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ.
&Gloria
R. $2
responsory3.eng:
R. O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise
* For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.
V. Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God. Let all that are making this holy memorial of thee feel the might of thine assistance.
R. For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Now let the earth with joy resound,
And heaven the chant re-echo round;
Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise
The great Apostles' glorious praise.
O ye who, throned in glory dread,
Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.
Ye close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.
Sickness and health your voice obey;
At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.
So when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.
* Praise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Exsúltet orbis gáudiis:
Cælum resúltet láudibus:
Apostolórum glóriam
Tellus et astra cóncinunt.
Vos sæculórum júdices,
Et vera mundi lúmina:
Votis precámur córdium,
Audíte voces súpplicum.
Qui templa cæli cláuditis,
Serásque verbo sólvitis,
Nos a reátu nóxios
Solvi jubéte, quǽsumus.
Præcépta quorum prótinus
Languor salúsque séntiunt:
Sanáte mentes lánguidas:
Augéte nos virtútibus.
Ut, cum redíbit árbiter
In fine Christus sǽculi,
Nos sempitérni gáudii
Concédat esse cómpotes.
* Patri, simúlque Fílio,
Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
Sicut fuit, sit júgiter
Sæclum per omne glória.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Th' eternal gifts of Christ the King,
The Apostles' glory, let us sing;
And all with hearts of gladness raise
Due hymns of thankful love and praise.
For they the Church's princes are,
Triumphant leaders in the war,
The heavenly King's own warrior band,
True lights to lighten every land.
Theirs was the steadfast faith of saints,
The hope that never yields nor faints,
The love of Christ in perfect glow,
That lay the prince of this world low.
In them the Father's glory shone,
In them the Spirit's will was done,
The Son himself exults in them;
Joy fills the new Jerusalem.
* Praise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Ætérna Christi múnera,
Apostolórum glóriam,
Palmas et hymnos débitos
Lætis canámus méntibus.
Ecclesiárum Príncipes,
Belli triumpháles duces,
Cæléstis aulæ mílites,
Et vera mundi lúmina.
Devóta Sanctórum fides,
Invícta spes credéntium,
Perfécta Christi cáritas
Mundi tyránnum cónterit.
In his Patérna glória,
In his triúmphat Fílius,
In his volúntas Spíritus,
Cælum replétur gáudio.
* Patri, simúlque Fílio,
Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
Sicut fuit, sit júgiter
Sæclum per omne glória.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Martyr of God, whose strength was steeled
To follow close God's only Son,
Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,
And well thy heavenly bliss was won!
Now join thy prayers with ours, who pray
That God may pardon us and bless;
For prayer keeps evil's plague away,
And draws from life its weariness.
Long, long ago, were loosed the chains
That held thy body once in thrall;
For us how many a bond remains!
O love of God release us all.
All praise to God the Father be,
All praise to thee, Eternal Son;
All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,
While never-ending ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Invícte Martyr, únicum
Patris secútus Fílium,
Victis triúmphas hóstibus,
Victor fruens cæléstibus.
Tui precátus múnere
Nostrum reátum dílue,
Arcens mali contágium,
Vitæ repéllens tǽdium.
Solúta sunt jam víncula
Tui sacráti córporis:
Nos solve vinclis sǽculi,
Dono supérni Núminis.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Deus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.
Hic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.
Pœnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.
Ob hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.
* Laus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
O God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.
He recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.
Bravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.
With humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.
* Glory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.
