lectio_prima.eng: He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
lectio_prima.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.

responsory_breve_nona.eng:
R.br. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
R. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
V. Honour and great majesty shalt Thou lay upon him.
R. In thy salvation.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
R.br. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.
R. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.
V. Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
R. In salutári tuo.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.

responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
R.br. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
R. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
V. A Crown of precious stones.
R. Upon his head.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
R.br. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.
R. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.
V. Corónam de lápide pretióso.
R. Super caput ejus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.

responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
R.br. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
R. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
V. And madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.
R. Thou hast crowned him.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
R.br. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.
R. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.
V. Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
R. Coronásti eum, Dómine.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.

tertia.capitulum.eng:
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
$Deo gratias
tertia.capitulum.lat:
Beátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
$Deo gratias

versum_1.eng:
V. The righteous shall flourish like the palm-tree.
R. He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
versum_1.lat:
V. Justus ut palma florébit.
R. Sicut cedrus Líbani multiplicábitur.

versum_2.eng:
V. Thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, O Lord.
R. And madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.
versum_2.lat:
V. Glória et honóre coronásti eum, Dómine.
R. Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Whosoever shall confess Me * before men, him will I confess also before My Father.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Qui me conféssus fúerit * coram homínibus, confitébor et ego eum coram Patre meo.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He that followeth Me * walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life, saith the Lord.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Qui séquitur me, * non ámbulat in ténebris, sed habébit lumen vitæ, dicit Dóminus.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: If any man serve Me, * let him follow Me and where I am, there shall also My servant be.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Qui mihi minístrat, * me sequátur: et ubi ego sum, illic sit et miníster meus.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: If any man serve Me, * him will My Father, who is in heaven, honour.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Si quis mihi ministráverit, * honorificábit eum Pater meus, qui est in cælis, dicit Dóminus.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Father, I will * that where I am, there shall also My servant be.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Volo Pater, * ut ubi ego sum, illic sit et miníster meus.

vesperae.capitulum.eng:
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
$Deo gratias
vesperae.capitulum.lat:
Beátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
$Deo gratias

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: In lege Dómini * fuit volúntas ejus die ac nocte.
ant_1.eng: His delight * was in the law of the Lord day and night.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
ant_2.eng: O ye sons of men, * know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Justus Dóminus, * et justítiam diléxit: æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
ant_3.eng: The righteous Lord * loveth righteousness; His countenance doth behold uprightness.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. O Lord, Thou hast set a crown of precious stones.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. His glory is great in thy salvation.
nocturn_3_versum.latR: ℟. Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. Honour and great majesty shalt Thou lay upon him.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: In lege Dómini * fuit volúntas ejus die ac nocte.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: His delight * was in the law of the Lord day and night.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Prǽdicans * præcéptum Dómini constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord hath set him * upon His holy hill, to declare His decree.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi: et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I cried unto the Lord * with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O ye sons of men, * know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Scuto bonæ voluntátis * tuæ coronásti eum Dómine.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: O Lord, Thou hast compassed him * with thy favour as with a shield.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: In univérsa terra * glória et honóre coronásti eum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour in all the earth.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Justus Dóminus, * et justítiam diléxit: æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: The righteous Lord * loveth righteousness; His countenance doth behold uprightness.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo: requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: He shall dwell * in thy tabernacle, He shall rest upon thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Posuísti, Dómine, * super caput ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: O Lord, Thou hast set a crown * of precious stones upon his head.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 1

verses.lat: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, † et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
verses.eng: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, † nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

verses.lat: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas ejus, * et in lege ejus meditábitur die ac nocte.
verses.eng: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

verses.lat: 1:3a Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
verses.eng: 1:3a And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

verses.lat: 1:3b Et fólium ejus non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
verses.eng: 1:3b And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

verses.lat: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
verses.eng: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

verses.lat: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in judício: * neque peccatóres in concílio justórum.
verses.eng: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

verses.lat: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam justórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
verses.eng: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: In lege Dómini * fuit volúntas ejus die ac nocte.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: His delight * was in the law of the Lord day and night.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 2

verses.lat: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
verses.eng: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

verses.lat: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

verses.lat: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis jugum ipsórum.
verses.eng: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

verses.lat: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

verses.lat: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

verses.lat: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, * prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

verses.lat: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
verses.eng: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

verses.lat: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
verses.eng: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

verses.lat: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
verses.eng: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

verses.lat: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui judicátis terram.
verses.eng: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

verses.lat: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
verses.eng: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

verses.lat: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via justa.
verses.eng: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

verses.lat: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira ejus: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
verses.eng: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Prǽdicans * præcéptum Dómini constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: The Lord hath set him * upon His holy hill, to declare His decree.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 3

verses.lat: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
verses.eng: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

verses.lat: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus.
verses.eng: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

verses.lat: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
verses.eng: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

verses.lat: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
verses.eng: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

verses.lat: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
verses.eng: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

verses.lat: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
verses.eng: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

verses.lat: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
verses.eng: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

verses.lat: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
verses.eng: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Voce mea * ad Dóminum clamávi: et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: I cried unto the Lord * with my voice, and He heard me out of His holy hill.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 4

verses.lat: 4:2a Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus justítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
verses.eng: 4:2a When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

verses.lat: 4:2b Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
verses.eng: 4:2b Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

verses.lat: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
verses.eng: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

verses.lat: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
verses.eng: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

verses.lat: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: ‡ quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, * in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
verses.eng: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: ‡ the things you say in your hearts, * be sorry for them upon your beds.

verses.lat: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium justítiæ, † et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
verses.eng: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, † and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

verses.lat: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
verses.eng: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

verses.lat: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
verses.eng: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

verses.lat: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
verses.eng: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

verses.lat: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
verses.eng: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: O ye sons of men, * know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 5

verses.lat: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
verses.eng: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

verses.lat: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

verses.lat: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
verses.eng: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

verses.lat: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
verses.eng: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

verses.lat: 5:6 Neque habitábit juxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt injústi ante óculos tuos.
verses.eng: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

verses.lat: 5:7a Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
verses.eng: 5:7a Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

verses.lat: 5:7b Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * (8a) ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 5:7b The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * (8a) But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

verses.lat: 5:8b Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
verses.eng: 5:8b I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

verses.lat: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in justítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
verses.eng: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

verses.lat: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
verses.eng: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

verses.lat: 5:11a Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, † linguis suis dolóse agébant, * júdica illos, Deus.
verses.eng: 5:11a Their throat is an open sepulchre: † they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

verses.lat: 5:11b Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, † secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 5:11b Let them fall from their devices: † according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 5:12a Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
verses.eng: 5:12a But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

verses.lat: 5:12b Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * (13a) quóniam tu benedíces justo.
verses.eng: 5:12b And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * (13a) For thou wilt bless the just.

verses.lat: 5:13b Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
verses.eng: 5:13b O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Scuto bonæ voluntátis * tuæ coronásti eum Dómine.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: O Lord, Thou hast compassed him * with thy favour as with a shield.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 8

verses.lat: 8:2a Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:2a O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

verses.lat: 8:2b Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
verses.eng: 8:2b For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

verses.lat: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
verses.eng: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

verses.lat: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
verses.eng: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

verses.lat: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es ejus? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
verses.eng: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

verses.lat: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, † glória et honóre coronásti eum: * (7) et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
verses.eng: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, † thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * (7) and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

verses.lat: 8:8 Ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
verses.eng: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

verses.lat: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
verses.eng: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

verses.lat: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: In univérsa terra * glória et honóre coronásti eum.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour in all the earth.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 10

verses.lat: 10:2 In Dómino confído: † quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?
verses.eng: 10:2 In the Lord I put my trust: † how then do you say to my soul: * Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow?

verses.lat: 10:3 Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, † paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
verses.eng: 10:3 For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow: † they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.

verses.lat: 10:4 Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * justus autem quid fecit?
verses.eng: 10:4 For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: * but what has the just man done?

verses.lat: 10:5a Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes ejus.
verses.eng: 10:5a The Lord is in his holy temple, * the Lord’s throne is in heaven.

verses.lat: 10:5b Óculi ejus in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ ejus intérrogant fílios hóminum.
verses.eng: 10:5b His eyes look on the poor man: * his eyelids examine the sons of men.

verses.lat: 10:6 Dóminus intérrogat justum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.
verses.eng: 10:6 The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: * but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.

verses.lat: 10:7 Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.
verses.eng: 10:7 He shall rain snares upon sinners: * fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup.

verses.lat: 10:8 Quóniam justus Dóminus, et justítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
verses.eng: 10:8 For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: * his countenance hath beheld righteousness.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Justus Dóminus, * et justítiam diléxit: æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: The righteous Lord * loveth righteousness; His countenance doth behold uprightness.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 14

verses.lat: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
verses.eng: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

verses.lat: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur justítiam:
verses.eng: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

verses.lat: 14:3a Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
verses.eng: 14:3a He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

verses.lat: 14:3b Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
verses.eng: 14:3b Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

verses.lat: 14:4a Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
verses.eng: 14:4a In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

verses.lat: 14:4b Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * (5a) qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
verses.eng: 14:4b He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * (5a) He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

verses.lat: 14:5b Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 14:5b He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Habitábit * in tabernáculo tuo: requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: He shall dwell * in thy tabernacle, He shall rest upon thy holy hill.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 20

verses.lat: 20:2 Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.
verses.eng: 20:2 The king rejoices in thy strength, O Lord; * and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.

verses.lat: 20:3 Desidérium cordis ejus tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.
verses.eng: 20:3 Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: * and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.

verses.lat: 20:4 Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
verses.eng: 20:4 For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: * thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.

verses.lat: 20:5 Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 20:5 He asked life of thee: * and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 20:6 Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
verses.eng: 20:6 His glory is great in thy salvation: * glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.

verses.lat: 20:7 Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi: * lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo.
verses.eng: 20:7 For thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever: * thou shalt make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance.

verses.lat: 20:8 Quóniam rex sperat in Dómino: * et in misericórdia Altíssimi non commovébitur.
verses.eng: 20:8 For the king hopeth in the Lord: * and through the mercy of the most High he shall not be moved.

verses.lat: 20:9 Inveniátur manus tua ómnibus inimícis tuis: * déxtera tua invéniat omnes, qui te odérunt.
verses.eng: 20:9 Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: * let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee.

verses.lat: 20:10 Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis in témpore vultus tui: * Dóminus in ira sua conturbábit eos, et devorábit eos ignis.
verses.eng: 20:10 Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, * in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.

verses.lat: 20:11 Fructum eórum de terra perdes: * et semen eórum a fíliis hóminum.
verses.eng: 20:11 Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth: * and their seed from among the children of men.

verses.lat: 20:12 Quóniam declinavérunt in te mala: * cogitavérunt consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre.
verses.eng: 20:12 For they have intended evils against thee: * they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.

verses.lat: 20:13 Quóniam pones eos dorsum: * in relíquiis tuis præparábis vultum eórum.
verses.eng: 20:13 For thou shalt make them turn their back: * in thy remnants thou shalt prepare their face.

verses.lat: 20:14 Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua: * cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas.
verses.eng: 20:14 Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy own strength: * we will sing and praise thy power.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Posuísti, Dómine, * super caput ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: O Lord, Thou hast set a crown * of precious stones upon his head.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: In lege Dómini * fuit volúntas ejus die ac nocte.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: His delight * was in the law of the Lord day and night.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Fílii hóminum * scitóte quia Dóminus sanctum suum mirificávit.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: O ye sons of men, * know that the Lord hath set apart him that is holy for Himself.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Justus Dóminus, * et justítiam diléxit: æquitátem vidit vultus ejus.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: The righteous Lord * loveth righteousness; His countenance doth behold uprightness.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Iste Sanctus pro lege Dei sui certávit usque ad mortem, et a verbis impiórum non tímuit:
* Fundátus enim erat supra firmam petram.
V. Iste est qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
R. Fundátus enim erat supra firmam petram.
responsory1.eng:
R. This man is holy, for he hath striven for the law of his God even unto death, and hath not feared for the words of the ungodly;
* For he had his foundation upon a strong rock.
V. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and is come unto an everlasting kingdom.
R. For he had his foundation upon a strong rock.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Justus germinábit sicut lílium:
* Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
V. Plantátus in domo Dómini, in átriis domus Dei nostri.
R. Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
responsory2.eng:
R. The righteous shall grow as the lily
* Yea, he shall flourish in the presence of the Lord for ever.
V. Those that be planted in the house of the Lord, shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
R. Yea, he shall flourish in the presence of the Lord for ever.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Iste cognóvit justítiam, et vidit mirabília magna, et exorávit Altíssimum
* Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
V. Iste est qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
R. Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
&Gloria
R. Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
responsory3.eng:
R. This is he which knew righteousness, and saw great wonders, and made his prayer unto the Most High
* And he is numbered among the Saints.
V. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and is come unto an everlasting kingdom.
R. And he is numbered among the Saints.
&Gloria
R. And he is numbered among the Saints.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Honéstum fecit illum Dóminus, et custodívit eum ab inimícis, et a seductóribus tutávit illum:
* Et dedit illi claritátem ætérnam.
V. Descendítque cum illo in fóveam, et in vínculis non derelíquit eum.
R. Et dedit illi claritátem ætérnam.
responsory4.eng:
R. The Lord made him honourable, and defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait for him,
* And gave him perpetual glory.
V. He went down with him into the pit, and left him not in bonds.
R. And gave him perpetual glory.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Desidérium ánimæ ejus tribuísti ei Dómine,
* Et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.
V. Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
R. Et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.
responsory5.eng:
R. Lord, Thou hast given him his heart's desire.
* And hast not withholden the request of his lips.
V. For Thou hast prevented him with the blessings of sweetness: Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.
R. And hast not withholden the request of his lips.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Stola jucunditátis índuit eum Dóminus:
* Et corónam pulchritúdinis pósuit super caput ejus.
V. Cibávit illum Dóminus pane vitæ et intelléctus: et aqua sapiéntiæ salutáris potávit illum.
R. Et corónam pulchritúdinis pósuit super caput ejus.
&Gloria
R. Et corónam pulchritúdinis pósuit super caput ejus.
responsory6.eng:
R. The Lord hath put on him a robe of honour,
* And put about his head a crown of joy.
V. With the bread of life and understanding hath the Lord fed him, and given him the water of health and wisdom to drink.
R. And put about his head a crown of joy.
&Gloria
R. And put about his head a crown of joy.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Coróna áurea super caput ejus,
* Expréssa signo sanctitátis, glória honóris, et opus fortitúdinis.
V. Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis, posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
R. Expréssa signo sanctitátis, glória honóris, et opus fortitúdinis.
responsory7.eng:
R. A crown of gold upon his head,
* Wherein is engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour, a costly work.
V. For Thou hast prevented him with the blessings of sweetness, Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.
R. Wherein is engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour, a costly work.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Hic est vere Martyr, qui pro Christi nómine sánguinem suum fudit:
* Qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit.
V. Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei.
R. Qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit.
&Gloria
R. Qui minas júdicum non tímuit, nec terrénæ dignitátis glóriam quæsívit, sed ad cæléstia regna pervénit.
responsory8.eng:
R. This is a Martyr indeed, who shed his blood for Christ's Name's sake
* Who feared not for the threats of judges, nor sought to be great with the glory of this world, but pressed on unto the kingdom of heaven.
V. The Lord guided the righteous in right paths, and showed him the kingdom of God.
R. Who feared not for the threats of judges, nor sought to be great with the glory of this world, but pressed on unto the kingdom of heaven.
&Gloria
R. Who feared not for the threats of judges, nor sought to be great with the glory of this world, but pressed on unto the kingdom of heaven.

ant_laudes.eng: He that hateth his life * in this world, shall keep it unto life eternal.
ant_laudes.lat: Qui odit * ánimam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam ætérnam custódit eam.

ant_vespera.eng: This man is holy * for he hath striven for the law of his God even unto death, and hath not feared for the words of the ungodly; For he had his foundation upon a strong rock.
ant_vespera.lat: Iste Sanctus * pro lege Dei sui certávit usque ad mortem, et a verbis impiórum non tímuit: fundátus enim erat supra firmam petram.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been proved, he shall receive a crown of life, which God hath promised to them that love him.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Beátus vir, qui suffert tentatiónem: quóniam cum probátus fúerit, accípiet corónam vitæ, quam repromísit Deus diligéntibus se.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
With the bread of life and understanding, she shall feed him, and give him the water of wholesome wisdom to drink: and she shall be made strong in him, and he shall not be moved.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Cibávit illum pane vitæ et intelléctus, et aqua sapiéntiæ salutáris potávit illum Dóminus Deus noster.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Martyr of God, whose strength was steeled
To follow close God's only Son,
Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,
And well thy heavenly bliss was won!
Now join thy prayers with ours, who pray
That God may pardon us and bless;
For prayer keeps evil's plague away,
And draws from life its weariness.
Long, long ago, were loosed the chains
That held thy body once in thrall;
For us how many a bond remains!
O love of God release us all.
All praise to God the Father be,
All praise to thee, Eternal Son;
All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,
While never-ending ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Invícte Martyr, únicum
Patris secútus Fílium,
Victis triúmphas hóstibus,
Victor fruens cæléstibus.
Tui precátus múnere
Nostrum reátum dílue,
Arcens mali contágium,
Vitæ repéllens tǽdium.
Solúta sunt jam víncula
Tui sacráti córporis:
Nos solve vinclis sǽculi,
Dono supérni Núminis.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Deus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.
Hic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.
Pœnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.
Ob hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.
* Laus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
O God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.
He recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.
Bravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.
With humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.
* Glory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Deus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.
Hic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.
Pœnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.
Ob hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.
* Laus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Whosoever shall confess Me * before men, him will I confess also before My Father.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Qui me conféssus fúerit * coram homínibus, confitébor et ego eum coram Patre meo.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He that followeth Me * walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life, saith the Lord.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Qui séquitur me, * non ámbulat in ténebris, sed habébit lumen vitæ, dicit Dóminus.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: If any man serve Me, * let him follow Me and where I am, there shall also My servant be.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Qui mihi minístrat, * me sequátur: et ubi ego sum, illic sit et miníster meus.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: If any man serve Me, * him will My Father, who is in heaven, honour.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Si quis mihi ministráverit, * honorificábit eum Pater meus, qui est in cælis, dicit Dóminus.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Father, I will * that where I am, there shall also My servant be.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Volo Pater, * ut ubi ego sum, illic sit et miníster meus.

lectio_prima.eng: He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
lectio_prima.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.

responsory_breve_nona.eng:
R.br. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
R. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
V. Honour and great majesty shalt Thou lay upon him.
R. In thy salvation.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. His glory is great * in thy salvation.
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
R.br. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.
R. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.
V. Glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
R. In salutári tuo.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Magna est glória ejus * In salutári tuo.

responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
R.br. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
R. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
V. A Crown of precious stones.
R. Upon his head.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. O Lord, Thou hast set * Upon his head.
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
R.br. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.
R. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.
V. Corónam de lápide pretióso.
R. Super caput ejus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Posuísti, Dómine, * Super caput ejus.

responsory_breve_tertia.eng:
R.br. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
R. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
V. And madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.
R. Thou hast crowned him.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. Thou hast crowned him * with glory and honour, O Lord.
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
R.br. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.
R. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.
V. Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
R. Coronásti eum, Dómine.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Glória et honóre * Coronásti eum, Dómine.

versum_1.lat:

R. Et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Martyr of God, whose strength was steeled
To follow close God's only Son,
Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,
And well thy heavenly bliss was won!
Now join thy prayers with ours, who pray
That God may pardon us and bless;
For prayer keeps evil's plague away,
And draws from life its weariness.
Long, long ago, were loosed the chains
That held thy body once in thrall;
For us how many a bond remains!
O love of God release us all.
All praise to God the Father be,
All praise to thee, Eternal Son;
All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,
While never-ending ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Invícte Martyr, únicum
Patris secútus Fílium,
Victis triúmphas hóstibus,
Victor fruens cæléstibus.
Tui precátus múnere
Nostrum reátum dílue,
Arcens mali contágium,
Vitæ repéllens tǽdium.
Solúta sunt jam víncula
Tui sacráti córporis:
Nos solve vinclis sǽculi,
Dono supérni Núminis.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Deus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.
Hic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.
Pœnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.
Ob hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.
* Laus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
O God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.
He recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.
Bravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.
With humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.
* Glory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Martyr of God, whose strength was steeled
To follow close God's only Son,
Well didst thou brave thy battlefield,
And well thy heavenly bliss was won!
Now join thy prayers with ours, who pray
That God may pardon us and bless;
For prayer keeps evil's plague away,
And draws from life its weariness.
Long, long ago, were loosed the chains
That held thy body once in thrall;
For us how many a bond remains!
O love of God release us all.
All praise to God the Father be,
All praise to thee, Eternal Son;
All praise, O Holy Ghost, to thee,
While never-ending ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Invícte Martyr, únicum
Patris secútus Fílium,
Victis triúmphas hóstibus,
Victor fruens cæléstibus.
Tui precátus múnere
Nostrum reátum dílue,
Arcens mali contágium,
Vitæ repéllens tǽdium.
Solúta sunt jam víncula
Tui sacráti córporis:
Nos solve vinclis sǽculi,
Dono supérni Núminis.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Deus tuórum mílitum
Sors, et córona, prǽmium,
Laudes canéntes Mártyris
Absólve nexu críminis.
Hic nempe mundi gáudia,
Et blanda fraudum pábula
Imbúta felle députans,
Pervénit ad cæléstia.
Pœnas cucúrrit fórtiter,
Et sústulit viríliter,
Fundénsque pro te sánguinem,
Ætérna dona póssidet.
Ob hoc precátu súpplici
Te póscimus, piíssime;
In hoc triúmpho Mártyris
Dimítte noxam sérvulis.
* Laus et perénnis glória
Patri sit, atque Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
O God, of those that fought thy fight,
Portion, and prize, and crown of light,
Break every bond of sin and shame
As now we praise thy martyr's name.
He recked not of the world's allure,
But sin and pomp of sin forswore:
Knew all their gall, and passed them by,
And reached the throne prepared on high.
Bravely the course of pain he ran,
And bare his torments as a man:
For love of thee his blood outpoured,
And thus obtained the great reward.
With humble voice and suppliant word
We pray thee therefore, holy Lord,
While we thy martyr's feast-day keep,
Forgive thy loved and erring sheep.
* Glory and praise for aye be done
To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Ghost, who reign on high,
One God, to all eternity.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
O glorious King of martyr hosts,
Thou crown that each confessor boasts,
Who leadest to celestial day
Those who have cast earth's joys away:
Thine ear in mercy, Saviour, lend,
While unto thee our prayers ascend;
And as we count their triumphs won,
Forgive the sins that we have done.
Martyrs in thee their triumphs gain,
From thee confessors grace obtain;
O'ercome in us the lust of sin,
That we thy pardoning love may win.
To thee who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Rex glorióse Mártyrum,
Coróna confiténtium,
Qui respuéntes térrea
Perdúcis ad cæléstia:
Aurem benígnam prótinus
Inténde nostris vócibus:
Trophǽa sacra pángimus:
Ignósce quod delíquimus.
Tu vincis inter Mártyres
Parcísque Confessóribus:
Tu vince nostra crímina,
Largítor indulgéntiæ.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
The martyrs' triumphs let us sing,
Their blood poured forth for Christ the King,
And while due hymns of praise we pay,
Our thankful hearts cast grief away.
The world its terrors urged in vain;
They recked not of the body's pain;
One step, and holy death made sure
The life that ever shall endure.
To flames the martyr saints are hailed;
By teeth of savage beasts assailed;
Against them, armed with ruthless brand
And hooks of steel, their torturers stand.
The mangled frame is tortured sore,
The holy life-drops freshly pour;
They stand unmoved amidst the strife,
By grace of everlasting life.
Redeemer, hear us of thy love,
That, with the martyr host above,
Hereafter, of thine endless grace,
thy servants also may have place.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Christo profúsum sánguinem,
Et Mártyrum victórias,
Dignámque cælo láuream
Lætis sequámur vócibus.
Terróre victo sǽculi,
Pœnísque spretis córporis,
Mortis sacræ compéndio
Vitam beátam póssident.
Tradúntur igni Mártyres,
Et bestiárum déntibus;
Armáta sævit úngulis
Tortóris insáni manus.
Nudáta pendent víscera,
Sanguis sacrátus fúnditur;
Sed pérmanent immóbiles,
Vitæ perénnis grátia.
Te nunc, Redémptor, quǽsumus,
Ut mártyrum consórtio
Jungas precántes sérvulos
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Sing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!
They, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.
Lord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.
While they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.
What joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!
Yet we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Sanctórum méritis ínclita gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Gliscens fert ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.
Hi sunt, quos fátue mundus abhórruit;
Hunc fructu vácuum, flóribus áridum
Contempsére tui nóminis ásseclæ
Jesu, Rex bone cǽlitum.
Hi pro te fúrias, atque minas truces
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
His cessit lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.
Cædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non quærimónia;
Sed corde impávido mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.
Quæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martýribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine fúlgidis
Cingunt témpora láureis.
Te, summa o Déitas, únaque póscimus;
Ut culpas ábigas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis; ut tibi glóriam,
Annórum in sériem, canant.
Amen.
