matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 1

verses.lat: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, † et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
verses.eng: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, † nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

verses.lat: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas ejus, * et in lege ejus meditábitur die ac nocte.
verses.eng: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

verses.lat: 1:3a Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
verses.eng: 1:3a And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

verses.lat: 1:3b Et fólium ejus non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
verses.eng: 1:3b And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

verses.lat: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
verses.eng: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

verses.lat: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in judício: * neque peccatóres in concílio justórum.
verses.eng: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

verses.lat: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam justórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
verses.eng: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Secus decúrsus aquárum * plantávit víneam justórum, et in lege Dómini fuit volúntas eórum.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: By the rivers of water * hath the Lord planted the vineyard of the righteous, and in His Law do they meditate day and night.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 2

verses.lat: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
verses.eng: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

verses.lat: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

verses.lat: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis jugum ipsórum.
verses.eng: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

verses.lat: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

verses.lat: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

verses.lat: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, * prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

verses.lat: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
verses.eng: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

verses.lat: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
verses.eng: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

verses.lat: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
verses.eng: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

verses.lat: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui judicátis terram.
verses.eng: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

verses.lat: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
verses.eng: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

verses.lat: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via justa.
verses.eng: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

verses.lat: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira ejus: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
verses.eng: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Tamquam aurum * in fornáce probávit eléctos Dóminus: et quasi holocáusta accépit eos in ætérnum.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: As gold in the furnace * hath the Lord tried His chosen ones, and received them for ever as a burnt-offering.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 3

verses.lat: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
verses.eng: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

verses.lat: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus.
verses.eng: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

verses.lat: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
verses.eng: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

verses.lat: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
verses.eng: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

verses.lat: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
verses.eng: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

verses.lat: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
verses.eng: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

verses.lat: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
verses.eng: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

verses.lat: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
verses.eng: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Si coram homínibus * torménta passi sunt, spes electórum est immortális in ætérnum.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Though the elect be punished * in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality for ever.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 14

verses.lat: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
verses.eng: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

verses.lat: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur justítiam:
verses.eng: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

verses.lat: 14:3a Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
verses.eng: 14:3a He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

verses.lat: 14:3b Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
verses.eng: 14:3b Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

verses.lat: 14:4a Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
verses.eng: 14:4a In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

verses.lat: 14:4b Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * (5a) qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
verses.eng: 14:4b He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * (5a) He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

verses.lat: 14:5b Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 14:5b He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Dabo Sanctis meis * locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: I will give unto My Saints a place * in the kingdom of My Father, every one by his own name, saith the Lord.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 15

verses.lat: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. ‡ (2) Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, * quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
verses.eng: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. ‡ (2) I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, * for thou hast no need of my goods.

verses.lat: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
verses.eng: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

verses.lat: 15:4a Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
verses.eng: 15:4a Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

verses.lat: 15:4b Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
verses.eng: 15:4b I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

verses.lat: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
verses.eng: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

verses.lat: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
verses.eng: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

verses.lat: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
verses.eng: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

verses.lat: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
verses.eng: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

verses.lat: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
verses.eng: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

verses.lat: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
verses.eng: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

verses.lat: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, † adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
verses.eng: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, † thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Sanctis, qui in terra sunt ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: To the Saints that are in the earth * Thou hast made all my counsels admirable.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 23

verses.lat: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
verses.eng: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

verses.lat: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
verses.eng: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

verses.lat: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
verses.eng: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

verses.lat: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
verses.eng: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

verses.lat: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
verses.eng: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
verses.eng: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

verses.lat: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Sancti qui sperant in Dómino, * habébunt fortitúdinem, assúment pennas ut áquilæ, volábunt, et non defícient.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: The Saints that wait upon the Lord * shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles, they shall fly and not faint.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 32

verses.lat: 32:1 Exsultáte, justi, in Dómino: * rectos decet collaudátio.
verses.eng: 32:1 Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: * praise becometh the upright.

verses.lat: 32:2 Confitémini Dómino in cíthara: * in psaltério decem chordárum psállite illi.
verses.eng: 32:2 Give praise to the Lord on the harp; * sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.

verses.lat: 32:3 Cantáte ei cánticum novum: * bene psállite ei in vociferatióne.
verses.eng: 32:3 Sing to him a new canticle, * sing well unto him with a loud noise.

verses.lat: 32:4 Quia rectum est verbum Dómini, * et ómnia ópera ejus in fide.
verses.eng: 32:4 For the word of the Lord is right, * and all his works are done with faithfulness.

verses.lat: 32:5 Díligit misericórdiam et judícium: * misericórdia Dómini plena est terra.
verses.eng: 32:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; * the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

verses.lat: 32:6 Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt: * et spíritu oris ejus omnis virtus eórum.
verses.eng: 32:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; * and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:

verses.lat: 32:7 Cóngregans sicut in utre aquas maris: * ponens in thesáuris abýssos.
verses.eng: 32:7 Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; * laying up the depths in storehouses.

verses.lat: 32:8 Tímeat Dóminum omnis terra: * ab eo autem commoveántur omnes inhabitántes orbem.
verses.eng: 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, * and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.

verses.lat: 32:9 Quóniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
verses.eng: 32:9 For he spoke and they were made: * he commanded and they were created.

verses.lat: 32:10 Dóminus díssipat consília géntium: * réprobat autem cogitatiónes populórum, et réprobat consília príncipum.
verses.eng: 32:10 The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; * and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.

verses.lat: 32:11 Consílium autem Dómini in ætérnum manet: * cogitatiónes cordis ejus in generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 32:11 But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: * the thoughts of his heart to all generations.

verses.lat: 32:12 Beáta gens, cujus est Dóminus, Deus ejus: * pópulus, quem elégit in hereditátem sibi.
verses.eng: 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: * the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.

verses.lat: 32:13 De cælo respéxit Dóminus: * vidit omnes fílios hóminum.
verses.eng: 32:13 The Lord hath looked from heaven: * he hath beheld all the sons of men.

verses.lat: 32:14 De præparáto habitáculo suo * respéxit super omnes, qui hábitant terram.
verses.eng: 32:14 From his habitation which he hath prepared, * he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.

verses.lat: 32:15 Qui finxit sigillátim corda eórum: * qui intéllegit ómnia ópera eórum.
verses.eng: 32:15 He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: * who understandeth all their works.

verses.lat: 32:16 Non salvátur rex per multam virtútem: * et gigas non salvábitur in multitúdine virtútis suæ.
verses.eng: 32:16 The king is not saved by a great army: * nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.

verses.lat: 32:17 Fallax equus ad salútem: * in abundántia autem virtútis suæ non salvábitur.
verses.eng: 32:17 Vain is the horse for safety: * neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.

verses.lat: 32:18 Ecce, óculi Dómini super metuéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia ejus:
verses.eng: 32:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: * and on them that hope in his mercy.

verses.lat: 32:19 Ut éruat a morte ánimas eórum: * et alat eos in fame.
verses.eng: 32:19 To deliver their souls from death; * and feed them in famine.

verses.lat: 32:20 Ánima nostra sústinet Dóminum: * quóniam adjútor et protéctor noster est.
verses.eng: 32:20 Our soul waiteth for the Lord: * for he is our helper and protector.

verses.lat: 32:21 Quia in eo lætábitur cor nostrum: * et in nómine sancto ejus sperávimus.
verses.eng: 32:21 For in him our heart shall rejoice: * and in his holy name we have trusted.

verses.lat: 32:22 Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos: * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
verses.eng: 32:22 Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, * as we have hoped in thee.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Justi autem * in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: The righteous live * for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 33

verses.lat: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus ejus in ore meo.
verses.eng: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

verses.lat: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
verses.eng: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

verses.lat: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen ejus in idípsum.
verses.eng: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

verses.lat: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
verses.eng: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

verses.lat: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
verses.eng: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

verses.lat: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus ejus salvávit eum.
verses.eng: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

verses.lat: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
verses.eng: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
verses.eng: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

verses.lat: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti ejus: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
verses.eng: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

verses.lat: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
verses.eng: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

verses.lat: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
verses.eng: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

verses.lat: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
verses.eng: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

verses.lat: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
verses.eng: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

verses.lat: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
verses.eng: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

verses.lat: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super justos: * et aures ejus in preces eórum.
verses.eng: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

verses.lat: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
verses.eng: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

verses.lat: 33:18 Clamavérunt justi, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
verses.eng: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

verses.lat: 33:19 Juxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
verses.eng: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

verses.lat: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes justórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
verses.eng: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

verses.lat: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
verses.eng: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

verses.lat: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt justum, delínquent.
verses.eng: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

verses.lat: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
verses.eng: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Tradidérunt * córpora sua in mortem, ne servírent idólis: ídeo coronáti póssident palmam.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: They gave up their bodies unto death * rather than serve idols and therefore have they crowns on their heads and palms in their hands.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 45

verses.lat: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adjútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

verses.lat: 45:6 Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur: * adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
verses.eng: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

verses.lat: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Ecce merces * Sanctórum copiósa est apud Deum: ipsi vero mórtui sunt pro Christo, et vivent in ætérnum.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Behold, how great with God is the reward * of His Saints; yea, they who died for Christ's sake shall live for ever and ever.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: Secus decúrsus aquárum * plantávit víneam justórum, et in lege Dómini fuit volúntas eórum.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: By the rivers of water * hath the Lord planted the vineyard of the righteous, and in His Law do they meditate day and night.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Dabo Sanctis meis * locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: I will give unto My Saints a place * in the kingdom of My Father, every one by his own name, saith the Lord.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Justi autem * in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: The righteous live * for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 109

verses.lat: 109:1a Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
verses.eng: 109:1a The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

verses.lat: 109:1b Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:1b Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

verses.lat: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

verses.lat: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
verses.eng: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

verses.lat: 109:4 Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
verses.eng: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

verses.lat: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
verses.eng: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

verses.lat: 109:6 Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
verses.eng: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

verses.lat: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
verses.eng: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Isti sunt Sancti, * qui pro testaménto Dei sua córpora tradidérunt, et in sánguine Agni lavérunt stolas suas.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: These men are holy, * for they have given up their bodies unto death for the sake of the covenant of their God, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 110

verses.lat: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio justórum, et congregatióne.
verses.eng: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

verses.lat: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes ejus.
verses.eng: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

verses.lat: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus ejus: * et justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, † miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * (5a) escam dedit timéntibus se.
verses.eng: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, † being a merciful and gracious Lord: * (5a) he hath given food to them that fear him.

verses.lat: 110:5b Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * (6) virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
verses.eng: 110:5b He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * (6) he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

verses.lat: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum ejus véritas, et judícium.
verses.eng: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

verses.lat: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta ejus: † confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
verses.eng: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: † confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

verses.lat: 110:9a Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
verses.eng: 110:9a He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

verses.lat: 110:9b (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen ejus: * (10a) inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
verses.eng: 110:9b (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * (10a) the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

verses.lat: 110:10b Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 110:10b A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Sancti per fidem * vicérunt regna, operáti sunt justítiam, adépti sunt repromissiónes.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: The Saints through faith subdued kingdoms, * wrought righteousness, obtained promises.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 111

verses.lat: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis ejus volet nimis.
verses.eng: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

verses.lat: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen ejus: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
verses.eng: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

verses.lat: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo ejus: * et justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et justus.
verses.eng: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

verses.lat: 111:5 Jucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, † dispónet sermónes suos in judício: * (6) quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
verses.eng: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: † he shall order his words with judgment: * (6) because he shall not be moved for ever.

verses.lat: 111:7a In memória ætérna erit justus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
verses.eng: 111:7a The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

verses.lat: 111:7b Parátum cor ejus speráre in Dómino, † (8) confirmátum est cor ejus: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
verses.eng: 111:7b His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: † (8) his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

verses.lat: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: † justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu ejus exaltábitur in glória.
verses.eng: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: † his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

verses.lat: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, † déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
verses.eng: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, † he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Sanctórum velut áquilæ * juvéntus renovábitur: florébunt sicut lílium in civitáte Dómini.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: The youth of the Saints shall be renewed * like the eagle's they shall grow as the lily in the city of the Lord.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 112

verses.lat: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

verses.lat: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória ejus.
verses.eng: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

verses.lat: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * (6) et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
verses.eng: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * (6) and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

verses.lat: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
verses.eng: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

verses.lat: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
verses.eng: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

verses.lat: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
verses.eng: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Abstérget Deus * omnem lácrimam ab óculis Sanctórum: et jam non erit ámplius neque luctus, neque clamor, sed nec ullus dolor: quóniam prióra transiérunt.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: God shall wipe away all tears from the eyes of His Saints * and there shall be no more sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain; for the former things are passed away.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 115

verses.lat: 115:1 Crédidi, propter quod locútus sum: * ego autem humiliátus sum nimis.
verses.eng: 115:1 I have believed, therefore have I spoken; * but I have been humbled exceedingly.

verses.lat: 115:2 Ego dixi in excéssu meo: * Omnis homo mendax.
verses.eng: 115:2 I said in my excess: * Every man is a liar.

verses.lat: 115:3 Quid retríbuam Dómino, * pro ómnibus, quæ retríbuit mihi?
verses.eng: 115:3 What shall I render to the Lord, * for all the things that he hath rendered to me?

verses.lat: 115:4 Cálicem salutáris accípiam: * et nomen Dómini invocábo.
verses.eng: 115:4 I will take the chalice of salvation; * and I will call upon the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 115:5 Vota mea Dómino reddam coram omni pópulo ejus: * (6) pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini mors sanctórum ejus:
verses.eng: 115:5 I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people: * (6) precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.

verses.lat: 115:7a O Dómine, quia ego servus tuus: * ego servus tuus, et fílius ancíllæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 115:7a O Lord, for I am thy servant: * I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid.

verses.lat: 115:7b Dirupísti víncula mea: ‡ (8) tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, * et nomen Dómini invocábo.
verses.eng: 115:7b Thou hast broken my bonds: ‡ (8) I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise, * and I will call upon the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 115:9 Vota mea Dómino reddam in conspéctu omnis pópuli ejus: * (10) in átriis domus Dómini, in médio tui, Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 115:9 I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people: * (10) in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.

vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: In cæléstibus regnis * Sanctórum habitátio est, et in ætérnum réquies eórum.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: In the heavenly kingdoms, * there is the dwelling of the Saints there shall be their rest for ever and ever.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Abstérget Deus omnem lácrimam ab óculis Sanctórum: et jam non erit ámplius neque luctus, neque clamor, sed nec ullus dolor:
* Quóniam prióra transiérunt.
V. Non esúrient, neque sítient ámplius, neque cadet super illos sol, neque ullus æstus.
R. Quóniam prióra transiérunt.
responsory1.eng:
R. God shall wipe away all tears from the eyes of His Saints, and there shall be no more sorrow, there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain;
* For the former things are passed away.
V. They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more, neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.
R. For the former things are passed away.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Viri sancti gloriósum sánguinem fudérunt pro Dómino, amavérunt Christum in vita sua, imitáti sunt eum in morte sua:
* Et ídeo corónas triumpháles meruérunt.
V. Unus spíritus, et una fides erat in eis.
R. Et ídeo corónas triumpháles meruérunt.
responsory2.eng:
R. These men are holy, who have gloriously shed their blood for the Lord's sake, yea, who loved Christ in their lives, and were made like unto Him in their flesh,
* And therefore they have earned crowns of victory.
V. One spirit, and one faith was in them.
R. And therefore they have earned crowns of victory.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Tradidérunt córpora sua propter Deum ad supplícia:
* Et meruérunt habére corónas perpétuas.
V. Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.
R. Et meruérunt habére corónas perpétuas.
&Gloria
R. Et meruérunt habére corónas perpétuas.
responsory3.eng:
R. They gave their bodies for God’s sake to death
* And gained the everlasting crown.
V. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.
R. And gained the everlasting crown.
&Gloria
R. And gained the everlasting crown.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Sancti tui, Dómine, mirábile consecúti sunt iter, serviéntes præcéptis tuis, ut inveniréntur illǽsi in aquis válidis:
* Terra appáruit árida: et in Mari Rubro via sine impediménto.
V. Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ, et torréntes inundavérunt.
R. Terra appáruit árida: et in Mari Rubro via sine impediménto.
responsory4.eng:
R. thy Saints, O Lord, have passed a wonderful way, serving thy commandments, that they might be found without hurt in the midst of the mighty waters.
* Dry land appeared, and, out of the Red Sea, a way without impediment.
V. He smote the rock, and the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed.
R. Dry land appeared, and, out of the Red Sea, a way without impediment.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Vérbera carníficum non timuérunt Sancti Dei, moriéntes pro Christi nómine:
* Ut herédes fíerent in domo Dómini.
V. Tradidérunt córpora sua propter Deum ad supplícia.
R. Ut herédes fíerent in domo Dómini.
responsory5.eng:
R. The Saints of God shrank not from the stripes of the executioners, but died for Christ's Name's sake
* That they might be made joint-heirs in the house of the Lord.
V. They gave their bodies for God's sake to death.
R. That they might be made joint-heirs in the house of the Lord.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Tamquam aurum in fornáce probávit eléctos Dóminus, et quasi holocáusti hóstiam accépit illos: et in témpore erit respéctus illórum:
* Quóniam donum et pax est eléctis Dei.
V. Qui confídunt in illum, intélligent veritátem, et fidéles in dilectióne acquiéscent illi.
R. Quóniam donum et pax est eléctis Dei.
&Gloria
R. Quóniam donum et pax est eléctis Dei.
responsory6.eng:
R. As gold in the furnace hath the Lord tried His chosen ones, and received them as a burnt-offering, and yet a while, and they shall be regarded;
* For the grace of God, and His peace, are with His chosen.
V. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him.
R. For the grace of God, and His peace, are with His chosen.
&Gloria
R. For the grace of God, and His peace, are with His chosen.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Propter testaméntum Dómini, et leges patérnas, Sancti Dei perstitérunt in amóre fraternitátis:
* Quia unus fuit semper spíritus in eis, et una fides.
V. Ecce quam bonum et quam jucúndum habitáre fratres in unum.
R. Quia unus fuit semper spíritus in eis, et una fides.
responsory7.eng:
R. Because of the covenant of the Lord, and the laws of their fathers, the Saints of God abode in brotherly love,
* For one spirit and one faith was ever in them.
V. Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
R. For one spirit and one faith was ever in them.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Sancti mei, qui in carne pósiti, certámen habuístis:
* Mercédem labóris ego reddam vobis.
V. Veníte benedícti Patris mei, percípite regnum.
R. Mercédem labóris ego reddam vobis.
&Gloria
R. Mercédem labóris ego reddam vobis.
responsory8.eng:
R. O ye My Saints, who, being in the flesh, didst have striving
* I will render unto you a reward of your labours.
V. Come, ye blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom
R. I will render unto you a reward of your labours.
&Gloria
R. I will render unto you a reward of your labours.

ant_laudes.eng: Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered: * fear not therefore; ye are of more value than many sparrows.
ant_laudes.lat: Vestri capílli cápitis * omnes numeráti sunt: nolíte timére: multis passéribus melióres estis vos.

ant_vespera.eng: For theirs is the Kingdom of heaven * who love not their lives in this world, and have attained unto the reward of the Kingdom, and have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb.
ant_vespera.lat: Istórum est enim * regnum cælórum qui contempsérunt vitam mundi, et pervenérunt ad prǽmia regni, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, but they are in peace.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Justórum ánimæ in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos torméntum mortis. Visi sunt óculis insipiéntium mori: illi autem sunt in pace.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds. They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Fulgébunt justi, et tamquam scintíllæ in arundinéto discúrrent. Judicábunt natiónes, et dominabúntur pópulis: et regnábit Dóminus illórum in perpétuum.
$Deo gratias.

capitulum_sexta.eng:
And she rendered to the just the wages of their labours, and conducted them in a wonderful way: and she was to them for a covert by day, and for the light of stars by night.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Réddidit Deus mercédem labórum sanctórum suórum, et dedúxit illos in via mirábili: et fuit illis in velaménto diéi, et in luce stellárum nocte.
$Deo gratias.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
O glorious King of martyr hosts,
Thou crown that each confessor boasts,
Who leadest to celestial day
Those who have cast earth's joys away:
Thine ear in mercy, Saviour, lend,
While unto thee our prayers ascend;
And as we count their triumphs won,
Forgive the sins that we have done.
Martyrs in thee their triumphs gain,
From thee confessors grace obtain;
O'ercome in us the lust of sin,
That we thy pardoning love may win.
To thee who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Rex glorióse Mártyrum,
Coróna confiténtium,
Qui respuéntes térrea
Perdúcis ad cæléstia:
Aurem benígnam prótinus
Inténde nostris vócibus:
Trophǽa sacra pángimus:
Ignósce quod delíquimus.
Tu vincis inter Mártyres
Parcísque Confessóribus:
Tu vince nostra crímina,
Largítor indulgéntiæ.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
The martyrs' triumphs let us sing,
Their blood poured forth for Christ the King,
And while due hymns of praise we pay,
Our thankful hearts cast grief away.
The world its terrors urged in vain;
They recked not of the body's pain;
One step, and holy death made sure
The life that ever shall endure.
To flames the martyr saints are hailed;
By teeth of savage beasts assailed;
Against them, armed with ruthless brand
And hooks of steel, their torturers stand.
The mangled frame is tortured sore,
The holy life-drops freshly pour;
They stand unmoved amidst the strife,
By grace of everlasting life.
Redeemer, hear us of thy love,
That, with the martyr host above,
Hereafter, of thine endless grace,
thy servants also may have place.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Christo profúsum sánguinem,
Et Mártyrum victórias,
Dignámque cælo láuream
Lætis sequámur vócibus.
Terróre victo sǽculi,
Pœnísque spretis córporis,
Mortis sacræ compéndio
Vitam beátam póssident.
Tradúntur igni Mártyres,
Et bestiárum déntibus;
Armáta sævit úngulis
Tortóris insáni manus.
Nudáta pendent víscera,
Sanguis sacrátus fúnditur;
Sed pérmanent immóbiles,
Vitæ perénnis grátia.
Te nunc, Redémptor, quǽsumus,
Ut mártyrum consórtio
Jungas precántes sérvulos
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Sing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!
They, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.
Lord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.
While they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.
What joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!
Yet we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Sanctórum méritis ínclita gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Gliscens fert ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.
Hi sunt, quos fátue mundus abhórruit;
Hunc fructu vácuum, flóribus áridum
Contempsére tui nóminis ásseclæ
Jesu, Rex bone cǽlitum.
Hi pro te fúrias, atque minas truces
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
His cessit lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.
Cædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non quærimónia;
Sed corde impávido mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.
Quæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martýribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine fúlgidis
Cingunt témpora láureis.
Te, summa o Déitas, únaque póscimus;
Ut culpas ábigas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis; ut tibi glóriam,
Annórum in sériem, canant.
Amen.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Tamquam aurum * in fornáce probávit eléctos Dóminus: et quasi holocáusta accépit eos in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: As gold in the furnace * hath the Lord tried His chosen ones, and received them for ever as a burnt-offering.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Si coram homínibus * torménta passi sunt, spes electórum est immortális in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Though the elect be punished * in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality for ever.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dabo Sanctis meis * locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: I will give unto My Saints a place * in the kingdom of My Father, every one by his own name, saith the Lord.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Sanctis, qui in terra sunt ejus, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: To the Saints that are in the earth * Thou hast made all my counsels admirable.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Sancti qui sperant in Dómino, * habébunt fortitúdinem, assúment pennas ut áquilæ, volábunt, et non defícient.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: The Saints that wait upon the Lord * shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles, they shall fly and not faint.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Justi autem * in perpétuum vivent, et apud Dóminum est merces eórum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: The righteous live * for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Tradidérunt * córpora sua in mortem, ne servírent idólis: ídeo coronáti póssident palmam.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: They gave up their bodies unto death * rather than serve idols and therefore have they crowns on their heads and palms in their hands.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Ecce merces * Sanctórum copiósa est apud Deum: ipsi vero mórtui sunt pro Christo, et vivent in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Behold, how great with God is the reward * of His Saints; yea, they who died for Christ's sake shall live for ever and ever.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
O glorious King of martyr hosts,
Thou crown that each confessor boasts,
Who leadest to celestial day
Those who have cast earth's joys away:
Thine ear in mercy, Saviour, lend,
While unto thee our prayers ascend;
And as we count their triumphs won,
Forgive the sins that we have done.
Martyrs in thee their triumphs gain,
From thee confessors grace obtain;
O'ercome in us the lust of sin,
That we thy pardoning love may win.
To thee who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Inténde nostris vócibus:
Trophǽa sacra pángimus:
Ignósce quod delíquimus.
Tu vincis inter Mártyres
Parcísque Confessóribus:
Tu vince nostra crímina,
Largítor indulgéntiæ.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
O glorious King of martyr hosts,
Thou crown that each confessor boasts,
Who leadest to celestial day
Those who have cast earth's joys away:
Thine ear in mercy, Saviour, lend,
While unto thee our prayers ascend;
And as we count their triumphs won,
Forgive the sins that we have done.
Martyrs in thee their triumphs gain,
From thee confessors grace obtain;
O'ercome in us the lust of sin,
That we thy pardoning love may win.
To thee who, dead, again dost live,
All glory, Lord, thy people give;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Rex glorióse Mártyrum,
Coróna confiténtium,
Qui respuéntes térrea
Perdúcis ad cæléstia:
Aurem benígnam prótinus
Inténde nostris vócibus:
Trophǽa sacra pángimus:
Ignósce quod delíquimus.
Tu vincis inter Mártyres
Parcísque Confessóribus:
Tu vince nostra crímina,
Largítor indulgéntiæ.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
The martyrs' triumphs let us sing,
Their blood poured forth for Christ the King,
And while due hymns of praise we pay,
Our thankful hearts cast grief away.
The world its terrors urged in vain;
They recked not of the body's pain;
One step, and holy death made sure
The life that ever shall endure.
To flames the martyr saints are hailed;
By teeth of savage beasts assailed;
Against them, armed with ruthless brand
And hooks of steel, their torturers stand.
The mangled frame is tortured sore,
The holy life-drops freshly pour;
They stand unmoved amidst the strife,
By grace of everlasting life.
Redeemer, hear us of thy love,
That, with the martyr host above,
Hereafter, of thine endless grace,
thy servants also may have place.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Christo profúsum sánguinem,
Et Mártyrum victórias,
Dignámque cælo láuream
Lætis sequámur vócibus.
Terróre victo sǽculi,
Pœnísque spretis córporis,
Mortis sacræ compéndio
Vitam beátam póssident.
Tradúntur igni Mártyres,
Et bestiárum déntibus;
Armáta sævit úngulis
Tortóris insáni manus.
Nudáta pendent víscera,
Sanguis sacrátus fúnditur;
Sed pérmanent immóbiles,
Vitæ perénnis grátia.
Te nunc, Redémptor, quǽsumus,
Ut mártyrum consórtio
Jungas precántes sérvulos
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Sing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!
God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,
Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,
While these heroes of Christ ye sing!
They, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;
Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;
Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,
Came forth strong in thy name, as King.
Lord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!
Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free
Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;
Earth's might never their souls could bend.
While they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,
No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;
Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,
Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.
What joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,
Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;
Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,
How pure now is their bliss above!
Yet we, Father on high, God of eternal might,
Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;
Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,
So our songs may be songs of love.
Amen.
hymnus_vespera.lat:
Sanctórum méritis ínclita gáudia
Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
Gliscens fert ánimus prómere cántibus
Victórum genus óptimum.
Hi sunt, quos fátue mundus abhórruit;
Hunc fructu vácuum, flóribus áridum
Contempsére tui nóminis ásseclæ
Jesu, Rex bone cǽlitum.
Hi pro te fúrias, atque minas truces
Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
His cessit lácerans fórtiter úngula,
Nec carpsit penetrália.
Cædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
Non murmur résonat, non quærimónia;
Sed corde impávido mens bene cónscia
Consérvat patiéntiam.
Quæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
Quæ tu Martýribus múnera prǽparas?
Rubri nam flúido sánguine fúlgidis
Cingunt témpora láureis.
Te, summa o Déitas, únaque póscimus;
Ut culpas ábigas, nóxia súbtrahas,
Des pacem fámulis; ut tibi glóriam,
Annórum in sériem, canant.
Amen.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Ecce merces * Sanctórum copiósa est apud Deum: ipsi vero mórtui sunt pro Christo, et vivent in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Behold, how great with God is the reward * of His Saints; yea, they who died for Christ's sake shall live for ever and ever.

ant_laudes.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, saith the Lord.
ant_laudes.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.

ant_vespera.eng: O thou Priest and Bishop, * thou worker of mighty works, thou good shepherd over God’s people, pray for us unto the Lord.
ant_vespera.lat: Sacérdos et Póntifex, * et virtútum ópifex, pastor bone in pópulo, ora pro nobis Dóminum.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
Behold an high priest, who in his days pleased God, and was found righteous, and in the time of wrath he was made a propitiation.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Ecce sacérdos magnus, qui in diébus suis plácuit Deo, et invéntus est justus: et in témpore iracúndiæ factus est reconciliátio.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. To execute the office of the priesthood, and to have praise, and to glorify his people in his name. He chose him out of all men living, to offer sacrifice to God, incense, and a good savour.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Fungi sacerdótio, et habére laudem in nómine ipsíus, et offérre illi incénsum dignum in odórem suavitátis.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
There was not found the like to him in glory, who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him. Therefore by an oath he gave him glory in his posterity, that he should increase in his people.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Non est invéntus símilis illi, qui conserváret legem Excélsi: ídeo jurejurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the world’s Redeemer, O hear;
thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:
Accept with gentlest love today
The prayers and praises that we pay.
The meek confessor of thy name
Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.
The world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.
Grant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.
* To thee, O Christ, our loving King,
All glory, praise, and thanks we bring:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu Redémptor ómnium,
Perpes coróna Prǽsulum,
In hac die cleméntius
Indúlgeas precántibus.
Tui sacri qua nóminis
Conféssor almus cláruit:
Hujus celébrat ánnua
Devóta plebs solémnia.
Qui rite mundi gáudia
Hujus cadúca réspuens,
Æternitátis prǽmio
Potítur inter Ángelos.
Hujus benígnus ánnue
Nobis sequi vestígia:
Hujus precátu, sérvulis
Dimítte noxam críminis.
* Sit Christe, Rex piíssime,
Tibi, Patríque glória,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.
Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.
Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.
Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.
Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.
Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.
His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Therefore the Lord assured him * by an oath that He would multiply his seed among His people.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ideo jurejurándo * fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O all ye Priests of God, * bless ye the Lord O all ye servants of the Lord, sing praises unto our God.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sacerdótes Dei, * benedícite Dóminum: servi Dómini, hymnum dícite Deo. Allelúja.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.

R. For ever.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. Thou art a Priest * for ever.

R.br. Tu es sacérdos * In ætérnum.
R. Tu es sacérdos * In ætérnum.

Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
