ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
ant_1.eng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
ant_2.eng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
ant_3.eng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. The Lord hath chosen him for a Priest unto Himself.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. To offer up unto Him the sacrifice of praise.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. Thou art a Priest for ever.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 1

verses.lat: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, † et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
verses.eng: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, † nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

verses.lat: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas ejus, * et in lege ejus meditábitur die ac nocte.
verses.eng: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

verses.lat: 1:3a Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
verses.eng: 1:3a And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

verses.lat: 1:3b Et fólium ejus non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
verses.eng: 1:3b And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

verses.lat: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
verses.eng: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

verses.lat: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in judício: * neque peccatóres in concílio justórum.
verses.eng: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

verses.lat: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam justórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
verses.eng: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 2

verses.lat: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
verses.eng: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

verses.lat: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

verses.lat: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis jugum ipsórum.
verses.eng: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

verses.lat: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

verses.lat: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
verses.eng: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

verses.lat: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus, * prǽdicans præcéptum ejus.
verses.eng: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

verses.lat: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
verses.eng: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

verses.lat: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
verses.eng: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

verses.lat: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
verses.eng: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

verses.lat: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui judicátis terram.
verses.eng: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

verses.lat: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
verses.eng: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

verses.lat: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via justa.
verses.eng: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

verses.lat: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira ejus: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
verses.eng: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 3

verses.lat: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
verses.eng: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

verses.lat: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus.
verses.eng: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

verses.lat: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
verses.eng: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

verses.lat: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
verses.eng: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

verses.lat: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
verses.eng: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

verses.lat: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
verses.eng: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

verses.lat: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
verses.eng: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

verses.lat: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
verses.eng: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 4

verses.lat: 4:2a Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus justítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
verses.eng: 4:2a When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

verses.lat: 4:2b Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
verses.eng: 4:2b Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

verses.lat: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
verses.eng: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

verses.lat: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
verses.eng: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

verses.lat: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: ‡ quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, * in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
verses.eng: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: ‡ the things you say in your hearts, * be sorry for them upon your beds.

verses.lat: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium justítiæ, † et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
verses.eng: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, † and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

verses.lat: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
verses.eng: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

verses.lat: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
verses.eng: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

verses.lat: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
verses.eng: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

verses.lat: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
verses.eng: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 5

verses.lat: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
verses.eng: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

verses.lat: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

verses.lat: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
verses.eng: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

verses.lat: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
verses.eng: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

verses.lat: 5:6 Neque habitábit juxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt injústi ante óculos tuos.
verses.eng: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

verses.lat: 5:7a Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
verses.eng: 5:7a Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

verses.lat: 5:7b Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * (8a) ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 5:7b The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * (8a) But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

verses.lat: 5:8b Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
verses.eng: 5:8b I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

verses.lat: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in justítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
verses.eng: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

verses.lat: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
verses.eng: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

verses.lat: 5:11a Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, † linguis suis dolóse agébant, * júdica illos, Deus.
verses.eng: 5:11a Their throat is an open sepulchre: † they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

verses.lat: 5:11b Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, † secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 5:11b Let them fall from their devices: † according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 5:12a Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
verses.eng: 5:12a But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

verses.lat: 5:12b Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * (13a) quóniam tu benedíces justo.
verses.eng: 5:12b And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * (13a) For thou wilt bless the just.

verses.lat: 5:13b Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
verses.eng: 5:13b O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 8

verses.lat: 8:2a Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:2a O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

verses.lat: 8:2b Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
verses.eng: 8:2b For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

verses.lat: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
verses.eng: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

verses.lat: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
verses.eng: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

verses.lat: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es ejus? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
verses.eng: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

verses.lat: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, † glória et honóre coronásti eum: * (7) et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
verses.eng: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, † thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * (7) and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

verses.lat: 8:8 Ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
verses.eng: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

verses.lat: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
verses.eng: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

verses.lat: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 14

verses.lat: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
verses.eng: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

verses.lat: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur justítiam:
verses.eng: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

verses.lat: 14:3a Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
verses.eng: 14:3a He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

verses.lat: 14:3b Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
verses.eng: 14:3b Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

verses.lat: 14:4a Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
verses.eng: 14:4a In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

verses.lat: 14:4b Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * (5a) qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
verses.eng: 14:4b He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * (5a) He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

verses.lat: 14:5b Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 14:5b He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 20

verses.lat: 20:2 Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.
verses.eng: 20:2 The king rejoices in thy strength, O Lord; * and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.

verses.lat: 20:3 Desidérium cordis ejus tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum ejus non fraudásti eum.
verses.eng: 20:3 Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: * and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.

verses.lat: 20:4 Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
verses.eng: 20:4 For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: * thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.

verses.lat: 20:5 Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 20:5 He asked life of thee: * and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 20:6 Magna est glória ejus in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
verses.eng: 20:6 His glory is great in thy salvation: * glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.

verses.lat: 20:7 Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi: * lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo.
verses.eng: 20:7 For thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever: * thou shalt make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance.

verses.lat: 20:8 Quóniam rex sperat in Dómino: * et in misericórdia Altíssimi non commovébitur.
verses.eng: 20:8 For the king hopeth in the Lord: * and through the mercy of the most High he shall not be moved.

verses.lat: 20:9 Inveniátur manus tua ómnibus inimícis tuis: * déxtera tua invéniat omnes, qui te odérunt.
verses.eng: 20:9 Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: * let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee.

verses.lat: 20:10 Pones eos ut clíbanum ignis in témpore vultus tui: * Dóminus in ira sua conturbábit eos, et devorábit eos ignis.
verses.eng: 20:10 Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, * in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.

verses.lat: 20:11 Fructum eórum de terra perdes: * et semen eórum a fíliis hóminum.
verses.eng: 20:11 Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth: * and their seed from among the children of men.

verses.lat: 20:12 Quóniam declinavérunt in te mala: * cogitavérunt consília, quæ non potuérunt stabilíre.
verses.eng: 20:12 For they have intended evils against thee: * they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.

verses.lat: 20:13 Quóniam pones eos dorsum: * in relíquiis tuis præparábis vultum eórum.
verses.eng: 20:13 For thou shalt make them turn their back: * in thy remnants thou shalt prepare their face.

verses.lat: 20:14 Exaltáre, Dómine, in virtúte tua: * cantábimus et psallémus virtútes tuas.
verses.eng: 20:14 Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy own strength: * we will sing and praise thy power.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 23

verses.lat: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
verses.eng: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

verses.lat: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
verses.eng: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

verses.lat: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
verses.eng: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

verses.lat: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
verses.eng: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

verses.lat: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
verses.eng: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
verses.eng: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

verses.lat: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam:
* Intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
V. Dómine, quinque talénta tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum.
R. Intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
responsory1.eng:
R. Well done, thou good and faithful servant, thou hast been faithful over a few things. I will make thee ruler over many things:
* Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.
V. Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents; behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.
R. Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Ecce sacérdos magnus, qui in diébus suis plácuit Deo:
* Ideo jurejurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
V. Benedictiónem ómnium géntium dedit illi, et testaméntum suum confirmávit super caput ejus.
R. Ideo jurejurándo fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
responsory2.eng:
R. Behold an high priest, who in his days pleased God
* Therefore the Lord assured him by an oath that He would multiply his seed among His people.
V. He hath made him a blessing unto all nations, and hath established His covenant upon his head.
R. Therefore the Lord assured him by an oath that He would multiply his seed among His people

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum:
* Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
V. Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo, Sede a dextris meis.
R. Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
&Gloria
R. Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
responsory3.eng:
R. The Lord hath sworn and will not repent
* Thou art a Priest for ever after the order of Melchisedek.
V. The Lord said unto my Lord Sit Thou at My right hand.
R.* Thou art a Priest for ever after the order of Melchisedek.
&Gloria
R. Thou art a Priest for ever after the order of Melchisedek.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Invéni David servum meum, óleo sancto meo unxi eum:
* Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei.
V. Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, et fílius iniquitátis non nocébit ei.
R. Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei.
responsory4.eng:
R. I have found David My servant, with My holy oil have I anointed him
* For My hand shall help him.
V. The enemy shall prevail nothing against him, nor the son of wickedness afflict him.
R. For My hand shall help him.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Pósui adjutórium super poténtem, et exaltávi eléctum de plebe mea:
* Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei.
V. Invéni David servum meum, óleo sancto meo unxi eum.
R. Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei.
responsory5.eng:
R. I have laid help upon one that is mighty, and have exalted one chosen out of My people
* For My hand shall help him.
V. I have found David My servant, with My holy oil have I anointed him.
R. For My hand shall help him.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Iste est, qui ante Deum magnas virtútes operátus est, et omnis terra doctrína ejus repléta est:
* Ipse intercédat pro peccátis ómnium populórum.
V. Iste est, qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
R. Ipse intercédat pro peccátis ómnium populórum.
&Gloria
R. Ipse intercédat pro peccátis ómnium populórum.
responsory6.eng:
R. This is he which wrought great wonders before God, and the whole earth is full of his teaching
* May he pray for all people, that their sins may be forgiven unto them
V. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and hath attained unto the kingdom of heaven.
R. May he pray for all people, that their sins may be forgiven unto them
&Gloria
R. May he pray for all people, that their sins may be forgiven unto them

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum: stolam glóriæ índuit eum,
* Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.
V. Induit eum Dóminus lorícam fídei, et ornávit eum.
R. Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.
responsory7.eng:
R. The Lord loved him and beautified him He clothed him with a robe of glory
* And crowned him at the gates of Paradise.
V. The Lord hath put on him the breast-plate of faith, and hath adorned him.
R. And crowned him at the gates of Paradise.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris:
* Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.
V. Vigiláte ergo, quia nescítis qua hora Dóminus vester ventúrus sit.
R. Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.
&Gloria
R. Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.
responsory8.eng:
R. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;
* And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.
V. Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.
R. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.
&Gloria
R. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

ant_laudes.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things, saith the Lord.
ant_laudes.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, dicit Dóminus.

ant_vespera.eng: O thou Priest and Bishop, * thou worker of mighty works, thou good shepherd over God’s people, pray for us unto the Lord.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the world’s Redeemer, O hear;
thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:
Accept with gentlest love today
The prayers and praises that we pay.
The meek confessor of thy name
Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.
The world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.
Grant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.
* To thee, O Christ, our loving King,
All glory, praise, and thanks we bring:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu Redémptor ómnium,
Perpes coróna Prǽsulum,
In hac die cleméntius
Indúlgeas precántibus.
Tui sacri qua nóminis
Conféssor almus cláruit:
Hujus celébrat ánnua
Devóta plebs solémnia.
Qui rite mundi gáudia
Hujus cadúca réspuens,
Æternitátis prǽmio
Potítur inter Ángelos.
Hujus benígnus ánnue
Nobis sequi vestígia:
Hujus precátu, sérvulis
Dimítte noxam críminis.
* Sit Christe, Rex piíssime,
Tibi, Patríque glória,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.
Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.
Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.
Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.
Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.
Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.
His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the world’s Redeemer, O hear;
thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:
Accept with gentlest love today
The prayers and praises that we pay.
The meek confessor of thy name
Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.
The world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.
Grant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.
* To thee, O Christ, our loving King,
All glory, praise, and thanks we bring:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Jesu Redémptor ómnium,
Perpes coróna Prǽsulum,
In hac die cleméntius
Indúlgeas precántibus.
Tui sacri qua nóminis
Conféssor almus cláruit:
Hujus celébrat ánnua
Devóta plebs solémnia.
Qui rite mundi gáudia
Hujus cadúca réspuens,
Æternitátis prǽmio
Potítur inter Ángelos.
Hujus benígnus ánnue
Nobis sequi vestígia:
Hujus precátu, sérvulis
Dimítte noxam críminis.
* Sit Christe, Rex piíssime,
Tibi, Patríque glória,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.
Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.
Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.
Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.
Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.
Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.
His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

capitulum_laudes.eng:

v. She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
$Deo gratias

$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:
Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.
Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.
All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.
Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.
In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.
Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.
* All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:
Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.
Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.
Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.
Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.
Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.
Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.
* Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.
Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.
Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.
Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.
Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.
Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.
His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
ant_1.eng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
ant_2.eng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
ant_3.eng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. The Lord hath chosen him for a Priest unto Himself.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. To offer up unto Him the sacrifice of praise.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. Thou art a Priest for ever.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Justus germinábit sicut lílium:
* Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
V. Plantátus in domo Dómini, in átriis domus Dei nostri.
R. Et florébit in ætérnum ante Dóminum.
responsory2.eng:
R. The righteous shall grow as the lily;
* Yea, he shall flourish in the presence of the Lord for ever.
V. Those that be planted in the house of the Lord, shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
R. Yea, he shall flourish in the presence of the Lord for ever.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Iste cognóvit justítiam, et vidit mirabília magna, et exorávit Altíssimum:
* Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
V. Iste est qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
R. Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
&Gloria
R. Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
responsory3.eng:
R. This is he which knew righteousness, and saw great wonders, and made his prayer unto the Most High;
* And he is numbered among the Saints.
V. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and is come unto an everlasting kingdom.
R. And he is numbered among the Saints.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Honéstum fecit illum Dóminus, et custodívit eum ab inimícis, et a seductóribus tutávit illum:
* Et dedit illi claritátem ætérnam.
V. Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei.
R. Et dedit illi claritátem ætérnam.
responsory4.eng:
R. The Lord made him honourable, and defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait for him;
* And gave him perpetual glory.
V. He went down with him into the pit, and left him not in bonds.
R. And gave him perpetual glory.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Amávit eum Dóminus, et ornávit eum: stolam glóriæ índuit eum,
* Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.
V. Índuit eum Dóminus lorícam fídei, et ornávit eum.
R. Et ad portas paradísi coronávit eum.
responsory5.eng:
R. The Lord loved him and beautified him; He clothed him with a robe of glory,
* And crowned him at the gates of Paradise.
V. The Lord hath put on him the breast-plate of faith, and hath adorned him.
R. And crowned him at the gates of Paradise.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Iste homo perfécit ómnia quæ locútus est ei Deus, et dixit ad eum: Ingrédere in réquiem meam:
* Quia te vidi justum coram me ex ómnibus géntibus.
V. Iste est, qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
R. Quia te vidi justum coram me ex ómnibus géntibus.
&Gloria
R. Quia te vidi justum coram me ex ómnibus géntibus.
responsory6.eng:
R. This is he which did according unto all that God commanded him; and God said unto him: Enter thou into My rest,
* For thee have I seen righteous before Me among all people.
V. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and is come unto an everlasting kingdom.
R. For thee have I seen righteous before Me among all people.
&Gloria
R. For thee have I seen righteous before Me among all people.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Iste est qui ante Deum magnas virtútes operátus est, et de omni corde suo laudávit Dóminum:
* Ipse intercédat pro peccátis ómnium populórum.
V. Ecce homo sine queréla, verus Dei cultor, ábstinens se ab omni ópere malo, et pérmanens in innocéntia sua.
R. Ipse intercédat pro peccátis ómnium populórum.
responsory7.eng:
R. This is he which wrought great wonders before God, and praised the Lord with all his heart.
* May he pray for all people, that their sins may be forgiven unto them.
V. Behold a man without blame, a worshipper of God in truth, keeping himself clean from every evil work, and abiding still in his innocency.
R. May he pray for all people, that their sins may be forgiven unto them.

And stood forever fast.

In fastings and in prayers,

Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

At his petition.

Now and forever.

Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:
Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.
Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.
All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.
Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.
In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.
Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.
* All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:
Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.
Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.
Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.
Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.
Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.
Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.
* Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.
Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.
Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.
Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.
Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.
Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.
Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.
Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.
His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.
Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.
They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.
We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.
* All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:
Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.
Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;
Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.
* Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!
Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.
Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.
Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.
Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.
Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.
Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.
Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.
Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.
Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.
They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.
We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.
* All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

Post te canéntes cúrsitant,

invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * et una de número prudéntum.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: This, is one which hath not known the sinful bed, * she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Hæc est quæ nescívit * torum in delícto: habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Come, O my chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: She is beautiful * among the daughters of Jerusalem.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Ista est speciósa * inter fílias Jerúsalem.

lectio_prima.eng: O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.
lectio_prima.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.

responsory_breve_nona.eng:
R.br. God hath chosen her, * and fore-chosen her.
R. God hath chosen her, * and fore-chosen her.
V. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.
R. And fore-chosen her.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. God hath chosen her, * and fore-chosen her.
responsory_breve_nona.lat:
R.br. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.
R. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.
V. In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.
R. Et præelégit eam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.

responsory_breve_sexta.eng:
R.br. God shall help her * with His countenance.
R. God shall help her * with His countenance.
V. God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved.
R. With His countenance.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. God shall help her * with His countenance.
responsory_breve_sexta.lat:
R.br. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.
R. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.
V. Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.

Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.

responsory_breve_tertia.eng:

V. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. In thy beauty.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
R. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.
responsory_breve_tertia.lat:
R.br. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
R. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
V. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
R. Et pulchritúdine tua.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
R. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.

tertia.capitulum.eng:
Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.
$Deo gratias
tertia.capitulum.lat:
Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.

ant_3.label: Antíphona

ant_3.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.
