matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Ante torum * hujus Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Sing for us again and again before this maiden's bed * the tender idylls of the play.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 8

verses.lat: 8:2a Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:2a O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

verses.lat: 8:2b Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
verses.eng: 8:2b For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

verses.lat: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
verses.eng: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

verses.lat: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
verses.eng: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

verses.lat: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es ejus? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
verses.eng: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

verses.lat: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, † glória et honóre coronásti eum: * (7) et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
verses.eng: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, † thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * (7) and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

verses.lat: 8:8 Ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
verses.eng: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

verses.lat: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
verses.eng: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

verses.lat: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
verses.eng: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 18

verses.lat: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum ejus annúntiat firmaméntum.
verses.eng: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

verses.lat: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
verses.eng: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

verses.lat: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
verses.eng: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

verses.lat: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
verses.eng: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

verses.lat: 18:6a In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
verses.eng: 18:6a He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

verses.lat: 18:6b Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * (7a) a summo cælo egréssio ejus:
verses.eng: 18:6b Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * (7a) his going out is from the end of heaven,

verses.lat: 18:7b Et occúrsus ejus usque ad summum ejus: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre ejus.
verses.eng: 18:7b And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

verses.lat: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
verses.eng: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

verses.lat: 18:9 Justítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
verses.eng: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

verses.lat: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * judícia Dómini vera, justificáta in semetípsa.
verses.eng: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

verses.lat: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
verses.eng: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

verses.lat: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
verses.eng: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

verses.lat: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? † ab occúltis meis munda me: * (14a) et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
verses.eng: 18:13 Who can understand sins? † from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * (14a) and from those of others spare thy servant.

verses.lat: 18:14b Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
verses.eng: 18:14b If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

verses.lat: 18:15a Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
verses.eng: 18:15a And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

verses.lat: 18:15b Dómine, adjútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
verses.eng: 18:15b O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Ante torum * hujus Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: Sing for us again and again before this maiden's bed * the tender idylls of the play.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 23

verses.lat: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
verses.eng: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

verses.lat: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
verses.eng: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

verses.lat: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
verses.eng: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

verses.lat: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
verses.eng: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

verses.lat: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
verses.eng: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
verses.eng: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

verses.lat: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 44

verses.lat: 44:2a Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
verses.eng: 44:2a My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

verses.lat: 44:2b Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
verses.eng: 44:2b My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

verses.lat: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, † diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: † grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

verses.lat: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
verses.eng: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

verses.lat: 44:5a Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
verses.eng: 44:5a With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

verses.lat: 44:5b Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 44:5b Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

verses.lat: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

verses.lat: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
verses.eng: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

verses.lat: 44:8 Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
verses.eng: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

verses.lat: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te (10a) fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
verses.eng: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which (10a) the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

verses.lat: 44:10b Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
verses.eng: 44:10b The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

verses.lat: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
verses.eng: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

verses.lat: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
verses.eng: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

verses.lat: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
verses.eng: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

verses.lat: 44:14 Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis (15a) circumamícta varietátibus.
verses.eng: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, (15a) clothed round about with varieties.

verses.lat: 44:15b Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
verses.eng: 44:15b After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

verses.lat: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
verses.eng: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

verses.lat: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
verses.eng: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

verses.lat: 44:18a Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 44:18a They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

verses.lat: 44:18b Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 44:18b Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 45

verses.lat: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adjútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

verses.lat: 45:6 Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur: * adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
verses.eng: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

verses.lat: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 47

verses.lat: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

verses.lat: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
verses.eng: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

verses.lat: 47:4 Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
verses.eng: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

verses.lat: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
verses.eng: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

verses.lat: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
verses.eng: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

verses.lat: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
verses.eng: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

verses.lat: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

verses.lat: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
verses.eng: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

verses.lat: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * justítia plena est déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

verses.lat: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ: * propter judícia tua, Dómine.
verses.eng: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus ejus.
verses.eng: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

verses.lat: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus: * et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
verses.eng: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

verses.lat: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
verses.eng: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 95

verses.lat: 95:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * cantáte Dómino, omnis terra.
verses.eng: 95:1 Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * sing to the Lord, all the earth.

verses.lat: 95:2 Cantáte Dómino, et benedícite nómini ejus: * annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
verses.eng: 95:2 Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: * shew forth his salvation from day to day.

verses.lat: 95:3 Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus, * in ómnibus pópulis mirabília ejus.
verses.eng: 95:3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles: * his wonders among all people.

verses.lat: 95:4 Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 95:4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: * he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.lat: 95:5 Quóniam omnes dii géntium dæmónia: * Dóminus autem cælos fecit.
verses.eng: 95:5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: * but the Lord made the heavens.

verses.lat: 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo in conspéctu ejus: * sanctimónia et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne ejus.
verses.eng: 95:6 Praise and beauty are before him: * holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.

verses.lat: 95:7 Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
verses.eng: 95:7 Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour: * bring to the Lord glory unto his name.

verses.lat: 95:8 Tóllite hóstias, et introíte in átria ejus: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 95:8 Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

verses.lat: 95:9 Commoveátur a fácie ejus univérsa terra: * dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit.
verses.eng: 95:9 Let all the earth be moved at his presence. * Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned.

verses.lat: 95:10 Étenim corréxit orbem terræ qui non commovébitur: * judicábit pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 95:10 For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: * he will judge the people with justice.

verses.lat: 95:11 Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra: commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: * gaudébunt campi, et ómnia quæ in eis sunt.
verses.eng: 95:11 Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fulness thereof: * the fields and all things that are in them shall be joyful.

verses.lat: 95:12 Tunc exsultábunt ómnia ligna silvárum a fácie Dómini, quia venit: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 95:12 Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice before the face of the Lord, because he cometh: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, * et pópulos in veritáte sua.
verses.eng: 95:13 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with his truth.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 96

verses.lat: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
verses.eng: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

verses.lat: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu ejus: * justítia, et judícium corréctio sedis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

verses.lat: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos ejus.
verses.eng: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

verses.lat: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
verses.eng: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

verses.lat: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
verses.eng: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

verses.lat: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli justítiam ejus: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam ejus.
verses.eng: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

verses.lat: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
verses.eng: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

verses.lat: 96:7 Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.
verses.eng: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

verses.lat: 96:8 Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Judæ, * propter judícia tua, Dómine:
verses.eng: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 96:9 Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

verses.lat: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
verses.eng: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

verses.lat: 96:11 Lux orta est justo, * et rectis corde lætítia.
verses.eng: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

verses.lat: 96:12 Lætámini, justi, in Dómino: * et confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus.
verses.eng: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 97

verses.lat: 97:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * quia mirabília fecit.
verses.eng: 97:1 Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * because he hath done wonderful things.

verses.lat: 97:1 Salvávit sibi déxtera ejus: * et brácchium sanctum ejus.
verses.eng: 97:1 His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, * and his arm is holy.

verses.lat: 97:2 Notum fecit Dóminus salutáre suum: * in conspéctu géntium revelávit justítiam suam.
verses.eng: 97:2 The Lord hath made known his salvation: * he hath revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles.

verses.lat: 97:3 Recordátus est misericórdiæ suæ, * et veritátis suæ dómui Israël.
verses.eng: 97:3 He hath remembered his mercy * and his truth toward the house of Israel.

verses.lat: 97:3 Vidérunt omnes términi terræ * salutáre Dei nostri.
verses.eng: 97:3 All the ends of the earth have seen * the salvation of our God.

verses.lat: 97:4 Jubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * cantáte, et exsultáte, et psállite.
verses.eng: 97:4 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; * make melody, rejoice and sing.

verses.lat: 97:5 Psállite Dómino in cíthara, in cíthara et voce psalmi: * in tubis ductílibus, et voce tubæ córneæ.
verses.eng: 97:5 Sing praise to the Lord on the harp, on the harp, and with the voice of a psalm: * with long trumpets, and sound of cornet.

verses.lat: 97:6 Jubiláte in conspéctu regis Dómini: * moveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: orbis terrárum, et qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 97:6 Make a joyful noise before the Lord our king: * let the sea be moved and the fulness thereof: the world and they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 97:8 Flúmina plaudent manu, simul montes exsultábunt a conspéctu Dómini: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 97:8 The rivers shall clap their hands, the mountains shall rejoice together at the presence of the Lord: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 97:9 Judicábit orbem terrárum in justítia, * et pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 97:9 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with equity.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
matutinum.ant_1.eng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 109

verses.lat: 109:1a Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
verses.eng: 109:1a The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

verses.lat: 109:1b Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:1b Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

verses.lat: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

verses.lat: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
verses.eng: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

verses.lat: 109:4 Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
verses.eng: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

verses.lat: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
verses.eng: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

verses.lat: 109:6 Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
verses.eng: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

verses.lat: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
verses.eng: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * et una de número prudéntum.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 112

verses.lat: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

verses.lat: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória ejus.
verses.eng: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

verses.lat: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * (6) et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
verses.eng: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * (6) and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

verses.lat: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
verses.eng: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

verses.lat: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
verses.eng: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

verses.lat: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
verses.eng: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 121

verses.lat: 121:1 Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
verses.eng: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

verses.lat: 121:3 Jerúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cujus participátio ejus in idípsum.
verses.eng: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

verses.lat: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
verses.eng: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in judício, * sedes super domum David.
verses.eng: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

verses.lat: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Jerúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
verses.eng: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

verses.lat: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
verses.eng: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

verses.lat: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
verses.eng: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

verses.lat: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
verses.eng: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Hæc est quæ nescívit * torum in delícto: habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: This, is one which hath not known the sinful bed, * she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 126

verses.lat: 126:1a Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
verses.eng: 126:1a Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

verses.lat: 126:1b Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
verses.eng: 126:1b Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

verses.lat: 126:2a Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
verses.eng: 126:2a It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

verses.lat: 126:2b Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * (3) ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
verses.eng: 126:2b When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * (3) behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

verses.lat: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
verses.eng: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

verses.lat: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
verses.eng: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: Come, O my chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 147

verses.lat: 147:1 Lauda, Jerúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
verses.eng: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

verses.lat: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
verses.eng: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

verses.lat: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
verses.eng: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

verses.lat: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo ejus.
verses.eng: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

verses.lat: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
verses.eng: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

verses.lat: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris ejus quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

verses.lat: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus ejus, et fluent aquæ.
verses.eng: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

verses.lat: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Jacob: * justítias, et judícia sua Israël.
verses.eng: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

verses.lat: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et judícia sua non manifestávit eis.
verses.eng: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Veni Sponsa Christi, áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum; pro cujus amóre sánguinem tuum fudísti,
* Et cum Ángelis in paradísum introísti.
V. Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum;  quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam.
R. Et cum Ángelis in paradísum introísti.
responsory1.eng:
R.br. Come, Bride of Christ, and take the everlasting crown, which the Lord hath prepared for thee, even for thee who for the love of Him hast shed thy blood;
* And art entered with Angels into His garden.
V. Come, O My chosen one, and I will establish My throne in thee, for the King hath reatly desired thy beauty
R. And art entered with Angels into His garden.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis,
* Proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
V. Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
R. Proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
responsory2.eng:
R. Grace is poured into thy lips, therefore;
* God hath blessed thee for ever.
V. In thy comeliness and thy beauty, go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. God hath blessed thee for ever.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua
* Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
V. Diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis, proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
R. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
&Gloria
R. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
responsory3.eng:
R. In thy comeliness and thy beauty;
* Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
V. Grace is poured into thy lips, therefore God hath blessed thee for ever.
R. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
&Gloria
R. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam:
* Et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
V. Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
R. Et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
responsory4.eng:
R. Because of truth, and meekness, and righteousness;
* And thy right hand shall lead thee wonderfully.
V. In thy comeliness, and thy beauty, go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. And thy right hand shall lead thee wonderfully.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Dilexísti justítiam, et odísti iniquitátem:
* Proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ.
V. Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et justítiam.
R. Proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ.
responsory5.eng:
R. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity;
* Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness.
V. Because of truth, and meekness, and righteousness.
R. Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Afferéntur Regi vírgines post eam, próximæ ejus;
* Afferéntur tibi in lætítia et exsultatióne.
V. Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua; inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
R. Afferéntur tibi in lætítia et exsultatióne.
&Gloria
R. Afferéntur tibi in lætítia et exsultatióne.
responsory6.eng:
R. After her shall virgins be brought unto the King, her fellows
* They shall be brought unto thee with gladness and rejoicing.
V. In thy comeliness and thy beauty, go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
R. They shall be brought unto thee with gladness and rejoicing.
&Gloria
R. They shall be brought unto thee with gladness and rejoicing.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Hæc est Virgo sápiens, quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit, quæ accéptis lampádibus sumpsit secum óleum:
* Et veniénte Dómino, introívit cum eo ad núptias.
V. Média nocte clamor factus est: Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei.
R. Et veniénte Dómino, introívit cum eo ad núptias.
responsory7.eng:
R. This is one of those wise virgins, whom the Lord found watching, for when she took her lamp, she took oil with her.
* And when the Lord came, she went in with him to the marriage.
V. At midnight there was a cry made: Behold, the Bridegroom cometh, go ye out to meet him.
R. And when the Lord came, she went in with him to the marriage.

responsory8.label: Responsorium

* Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei.
V. Prudéntes vírgines, aptáte vestras lámpades.
R. Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei.

R. Ecce sponsus venit, exíte óbviam ei.

* Behold, the Bridegroom cometh, go ye out to meet him.

v. O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

capitulum_sexta.eng:
For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Æmulor enim vos Dei æmulatióne. Despóndi enim vos uni viro vírginem castam exhibére Christo.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.
Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.
They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.
We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.
* All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:
Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.
Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;
Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.
* Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!
Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.
Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.
Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.
Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.
Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.
Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.
Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.
Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.
Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.
They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.
We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.
* All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:
Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.
Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;
Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.
* Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis festum cánimus beátæ,
Accipe votum.

Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Æmulor enim vos Dei æmulatióne. Despóndi enim vos uni viro vírginem castam exhibére Christo.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.
Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.
They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.
We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.
* All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:
Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.
Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;
Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.
* Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.

So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

Praise with thanksgiving.
Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,

Amen.

Péctore carmen.

Amen.

ant_laudes.eng: Give her of the fruit of her hands, * and let her own works praise her in the gates.
ant_laudes.lat: Date ei * de fructu mánuum suárum, et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.

ant_vespera.eng: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchantman * seeking goodly pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
ant_vespera.lat: Símile est regnum cælórum * hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. My soul shall praise the Lord even to death. How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations!
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, et líberas eos de manu angústiæ, Dómine, Deus noster.
$Deo gratias.

capitulum_sexta.eng:
And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de multis tribulatiónibus quæ circumdedérunt me.
$Deo gratias.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
High let us all our voices raise
In that heroic woman's praise
Whose name, with saintly glory bright,
Shines in the starry realms of light.
Filled with a pure celestial glow,
She spurned all love of things below;
And heedless here on earth to stay,
Climbed to the skies her toilsome way.
With fasts her body she subdued,
But filled her soul with prayer's sweet food:
In other worlds she tastes the bliss
For which she left the joys of this.
O Christ, the strength of all the strong;
To whom our holiest deeds belong!
Through her prevailing prayers on high,
In mercy hear thy people's cry!
* To God the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Be glory while the ages flow,
From all above, and all below.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Fortem viríli péctore
Laudémus omnes féminam,
Quæ sanctitátis glória
Ubíque fulget ínclita.
Hæc sancto amóre sáucia,
Dum mundi amórem nóxium
Horréscit, ad cæléstia
Iter perégit árduum.
Carnem domans jejúniis,
Dulcíque mentem pábulo
Oratiónis nútriens,
Cæli potítur gáudiis.
Rex Christe, virtus fórtium,
Qui magna solus éfficis,
Hujus precátu, quǽsumus,
Audi benígnus súpplices.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Jam hiems tránsiit, * imber ábiit et recéssit: surge, amíca mea, et veni.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Come, O My chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee. Alleluia.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: She is beautiful * among the daughters of Jerusalem.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Ista est speciósa * inter fílias Jerúsalem.

vesperae.capitulum.eng:
Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.
$Deo gratias
vesperae.capitulum.lat:
Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.
$Deo gratias

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
ant_1.eng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
ant_2.eng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
ant_3.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. God shall help her with His countenance.
nocturn_2_versum.latR: ℟. Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. God is in the midst of her she shall not be moved.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
nocturn_3_versum.latR: ℟. In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Ante torum * hujus Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Sing for us again and again before this maiden's bed * the tender idylls of the play.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 109

verses.lat: 109:1a Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
verses.eng: 109:1a The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

verses.lat: 109:1b Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:1b Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

verses.lat: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

verses.lat: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
verses.eng: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

verses.lat: 109:4 Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
verses.eng: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

verses.lat: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
verses.eng: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

verses.lat: 109:6 Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
verses.eng: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

verses.lat: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
verses.eng: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Dum esset Rex * in accúbitu suo, nardus mea dedit odórem suavitátis.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: While the King sitteth at his table, * my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 112

verses.lat: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

verses.lat: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória ejus.
verses.eng: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

verses.lat: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * (6) et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
verses.eng: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * (6) and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

verses.lat: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
verses.eng: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

verses.lat: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
verses.eng: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

verses.lat: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
verses.eng: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: In odórem * unguentórum tuórum cúrrimus: adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te nimis.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: We will run after thee, * in the savour of thy good ointments. The virgins love them exceedingly.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 121

verses.lat: 121:1 Lætátus sum in his, quæ dicta sunt mihi: * In domum Dómini íbimus.
verses.eng: 121:1 I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: * We shall go into the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: 121:2 Stantes erant pedes nostri, * in átriis tuis, Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 121:2 Our feet were standing * in thy courts, O Jerusalem.

verses.lat: 121:3 Jerúsalem, quæ ædificátur ut cívitas: * cujus participátio ejus in idípsum.
verses.eng: 121:3 Jerusalem, which is built as a city, * which is compact together.

verses.lat: 121:4 Illuc enim ascendérunt tribus, tribus Dómini: * testimónium Israël ad confiténdum nómini Dómini.
verses.eng: 121:4 For thither did the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord: * the testimony of Israel, to praise the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 121:5 Quia illic sedérunt sedes in judício, * sedes super domum David.
verses.eng: 121:5 Because their seats have sat in judgment, * seats upon the house of David.

verses.lat: 121:6 Rogáte quæ ad pacem sunt Jerúsalem: * et abundántia diligéntibus te:
verses.eng: 121:6 Pray ye for the things that are for the peace of Jerusalem: * and abundance for them that love thee.

verses.lat: 121:7 Fiat pax in virtúte tua: * et abundántia in túrribus tuis.
verses.eng: 121:7 Let peace be in thy strength: * and abundance in thy towers.

verses.lat: 121:8 Propter fratres meos, et próximos meos, * loquébar pacem de te:
verses.eng: 121:8 For the sake of my brethren, and of my neighbours, * I spoke peace of thee.

verses.lat: 121:9 Propter domum Dómini, Dei nostri, * quæsívi bona tibi.
verses.eng: 121:9 Because of the house of the Lord our God, * I have sought good things for thee.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Jam hiems tránsiit, * imber ábiit et recéssit: surge, amíca mea, et veni.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: Lo the winter is past, * the rain is over and gone. Rise up, my love, and come away.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 126

verses.lat: 126:1a Nisi Dóminus ædificáverit domum, * in vanum laboravérunt qui ædíficant eam.
verses.eng: 126:1a Unless the Lord build the house, * they labour in vain that build it.

verses.lat: 126:1b Nisi Dóminus custodíerit civitátem, * frustra vígilat qui custódit eam.
verses.eng: 126:1b Unless the Lord keep the city, * he watcheth in vain that keepeth it.

verses.lat: 126:2a Vanum est vobis ante lucem súrgere: * súrgite postquam sedéritis, qui manducátis panem dolóris.
verses.eng: 126:2a It is vain for you to rise before light, * rise ye after you have sitten, you that eat the bread of sorrow.

verses.lat: 126:2b Cum déderit diléctis suis somnum: * (3) ecce heréditas Dómini fílii: merces, fructus ventris.
verses.eng: 126:2b When he shall give sleep to his beloved, * (3) behold the inheritance of the Lord are children: the reward, the fruit of the womb.

verses.lat: 126:4 Sicut sagíttæ in manu poténtis: * ita fílii excussórum.
verses.eng: 126:4 As arrows in the hand of the mighty, * so the children of them that have been shaken.

verses.lat: 126:5 Beátus vir, qui implévit desidérium suum ex ipsis: * non confundétur cum loquétur inimícis suis in porta.
verses.eng: 126:5 Blessed is the man that hath filled the desire with them; * he shall not be confounded when he shall speak to his enemies in the gate.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: Come, O My chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee. Alleluia.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 147

verses.lat: 147:1 Lauda, Jerúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
verses.eng: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

verses.lat: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
verses.eng: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

verses.lat: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
verses.eng: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

verses.lat: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo ejus.
verses.eng: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

verses.lat: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
verses.eng: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

verses.lat: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris ejus quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

verses.lat: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus ejus, et fluent aquæ.
verses.eng: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

verses.lat: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Jacob: * justítias, et judícia sua Israël.
verses.eng: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

verses.lat: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et judícia sua non manifestávit eis.
verses.eng: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Ista est speciósa * inter fílias Jerúsalem.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: She is beautiful * among the daughters of Jerusalem.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Fallax grátia, et vana est pulchritúdo: 
* Múlier timens Dóminum, ipsa laudábitur.
V. Date ei de fructu mánuum suárum, et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.
R. Múlier timens Dóminum, ipsa laudábitur.
&Gloria
R. Múlier timens Dóminum, ipsa laudábitur.
responsory6.eng:
R. Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain
* A woman that feareth God she shall be praised.
V. Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her own works praise her in the gates.
R. A woman that feareth God she shall be praised.
&Gloria
R. A woman that feareth God she shall be praised.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Os suum apéruit sapiéntiæ, et lex cleméntiæ in lingua ejus: considerávit sémitas domus suæ, 
* Et panem otiósa non comédit.
V. Gustávit et vidit quia bona est negotiátio ejus: non exstinguétur in nocte lucérna ejus.
R. Et panem otiósa non comédit.
responsory7.eng:
R. She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. She looketh well to the ways of her household
* And eateth not the bread of idleness.
V. She tasteth and perceiveth that her merchandise is good. Her candle goeth not out by night.
R. And she eateth not the bread of idleness.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Regnum mundi et omnem ornátum sǽculi contémpsi, propter amórem Dómini mei Jesu Christi: 
* Quem vidi, quem amávi, in quem crédidi, quem diléxi.
V. Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: dico ego ópera mea Regi.
R. Quem vidi, quem amávi, in quem crédidi, quem diléxi.
&Gloria
R. Quem vidi, quem amávi, in quem crédidi, quem diléxi.
responsory8.eng:
R. The kingdom of this world and all the beauty of life I have esteemed as nothing, for the excellency of the love of Jesus Christ my Lord
* Whom, having seen, I loved Whom, having believed, I longed after.
V. My heart is overflowing with a good matter I speak of my works unto the King.
R. Whom, having seen, I loved Whom, having believed, I longed after.
&Gloria
R. Whom, having seen, I loved Whom, having believed, I longed after.

ant_laudes.eng: Give her of the fruit of her hands, * and let her own works praise her in the gates.
ant_laudes.lat: Date ei * de fructu mánuum suárum, et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.

ant_vespera.eng: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchantman * seeking goodly pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
ant_vespera.lat: Símile est regnum cælórum * hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
Who shall find a valiant woman? Far and from the uttermost coasts is the price of her. The heart of her husband trusteth in her, and he shall have no need of spoils.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Mulíerem fortem quis invéniet? Procul et de últimis fínibus prétium ejus. Confídit in ea cor viri sui, et spóliis non indigébit.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. Many daughters have gathered together riches: thou hast surpassed them all. Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: the woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Multæ fíliæ congregavérunt divítias: tu supergréssa es univérsas. Fallax grátia, et vana est pulchritúdo: múlier timens Dóminum, ipsa laudábitur.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
She hath opened her hand to the needy, and stretched out her hands to the poor. She shall not fear for her house in the cold of snow.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Manum suam apéruit ínopi, et palmas suas exténdit ad páuperem. Non timébit dómui suæ a frigóribus nivis.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
High let us all our voices raise
In that heroic woman's praise
Whose name, with saintly glory bright,
Shines in the starry realms of light.
Filled with a pure celestial glow,
She spurned all love of things below;
And heedless here on earth to stay,
Climbed to the skies her toilsome way.
With fasts her body she subdued,
But filled her soul with prayer's sweet food:
In other worlds she tastes the bliss
For which she left the joys of this.
O Christ, the strength of all the strong;
To whom our holiest deeds belong!
Through her prevailing prayers on high,
In mercy hear thy people's cry!
* To God the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Be glory while the ages flow,
From all above, and all below.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Fortem viríli péctore
Laudémus omnes féminam,
Quæ sanctitátis glória
Ubíque fulget ínclita.
Hæc sancto amóre sáucia,
Dum mundi amórem nóxium
Horréscit, ad cæléstia
Iter perégit árduum.
Carnem domans jejúniis,
Dulcíque mentem pábulo
Oratiónis nútriens,
Cæli potítur gáudiis.
Rex Christe, virtus fórtium,
Qui magna solus éfficis,
Hujus precátu, quǽsumus,
Audi benígnus súpplices.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!
Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.
Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.
Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.
Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.
Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.
Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.
Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.
Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. My soul shall praise the Lord even to death. How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations!
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, et líberas eos de manu angústiæ, Dómine, Deus noster.
$Deo gratias.

capitulum_sexta.eng:
And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de multis tribulatiónibus quæ circumdedérunt me.
$Deo gratias.

hymnus_laudes.eng:
High let us all our voices raise
In that heroic woman's praise
Whose name, with saintly glory bright,
Shines in the starry realms of light.
Filled with a pure celestial glow,
She spurned all love of things below;
And heedless here on earth to stay,
Climbed to the skies her toilsome way.
With fasts her body she subdued,
But filled her soul with prayer's sweet food:
In other worlds she tastes the bliss
For which she left the joys of this.
O Christ, the strength of all the strong;
To whom our holiest deeds belong!
Through her prevailing prayers on high,
In mercy hear thy people's cry!
* To God the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Be glory while the ages flow,
From all above, and all below.
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Fortem viríli péctore
Laudémus omnes féminam,
Quæ sanctitátis glória
Ubíque fulget ínclita.
Hæc sancto amóre sáucia,
Dum mundi amórem nóxium
Horréscit, ad cæléstia
Iter perégit árduum.
Carnem domans jejúniis,
Dulcíque mentem pábulo
Oratiónis nútriens,
Cæli potítur gáudiis.
Rex Christe, virtus fórtium,
Qui magna solus éfficis,
Hujus precátu, quǽsumus,
Audi benígnus súpplices.
* Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!
Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.
Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.
Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.
Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.
hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.
Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.
Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.
Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.
Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.
