nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
nocturn_3_versum.latR: ℟. In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Ante torum * hujus Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Sing for us again and again before this maiden's bed * the tender idylls of the play.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

ant_laudes.eng: Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at thy house. * And he made haste and came down, and received Him joyfully into his house. This day is salvation come from God to this house. Alleluia.
ant_laudes.lat: Zachǽe, * festínans descénde, quia hódie in domo tua opórtet me manére. At ille festínans descéndit, et suscépit illum gaudens in domum suam. Hódie huic dómui salus a Deo facta est, allelúja.

ant_vespera.eng: The Most High hath hallowed His Tabernacle. * For this is the House of God, whereon His Name shall be called, whereof it is written My Name shall be there, saith the Lord.
ant_vespera.lat: Sanctificávit Dóminus * tabernáculum suum: quia hæc est domus Dei, in qua invocábitur nomen ejus, de quo scriptum est: Et erit nomen meum ibi, dicit Dóminus.

capitulum_laudes.eng:
I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a Bride adorned for her husband.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_laudes.lat:
Vidi civitátem sanctam, Jerúsalem novam, descendéntem de cælo a Deo, parátam sicut sponsam ornátam viro suo.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_nona.eng:
v. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes, and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain; for the former things are passed away. And He That sat upon the throne said: Behold, I make all things new.
$Deo gratias.
capitulum_nona.lat:
Et abstérget Deus omnem lácrimam ab óculis eórum: et mors ultra non erit, neque luctus, neque clamor, neque dolor erit ultra, quia prima abiérunt. Et dixit qui sedébat in throno: Ecce nova fácio ómnia.
$Deo gratias

capitulum_sexta.eng:
And I heard a great voice out of the throne, saying Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them. And they shall be His people; and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God.
$Deo gratias
capitulum_sexta.lat:
Et audívi vocem magnam de throno dicéntem: Ecce tabernáculum Dei cum homínibus, et habitábit cum eis; et ipsi pópulus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis erit eórum Deus.
$Deo gratias

hymnus_laudes.eng:
From highest heaven, the Father's Son,
Descending like that mystic stone
Cut from a mountain without hands,
Came down below, and filled all lands;
Uniting, midway in the sky,
His house on earth, and house on high.
That house on high,  it ever rings
With praises of the King of kings;
Forever there, on harps divine,
They hymn th' eternal One and Trine;
We, here below, the strain prolong,
And faintly echo Sion's song.
O Lord of lords invisible!
With thy pure light this temple fill:
Hither, oft as invoked, descend;
Here to thy people's prayer attend;
Here, through all hearts, forevermore,
thy Spirit's quick'ning graces pour.
Here may the faithful, day by day,
Their hearts' adoring homage pay;
And here receive from thy dear love
The blessings of that home above;
Till loosened from this mortal chain,
Its everlasting joys they gain.
To God the Father, glory due
Be paid by all the heavenly host;
And to his only Son most true;
With thee, O mighty Holy Ghost!
To whom, praise, power, and blessing be,
Through th' ages of eternity,
Amen.
hymnus_laudes.lat:
Alto ex Olýmpi vértice
Summi Paréntis Fílius,
Ceu monte deséctus lapis
Terras in imas décidens,
Domus supérnæ et ínfimæ
Utrúmque junxit ángulum.
Sed illa sedes cǽlitum
Semper resúltat láudibus,
Deúmque trinum et únicum
Jugi canóre prǽdicat:
Illi canéntes júngimur
Almæ Siónis ǽmuli.
Hæc templa, Rex cæléstium,
Imple benígno lúmine:
Huc, o rogátus, ádveni,
Plebísque vota súscipe,
Et nostra corda júgiter
Perfúnde cæli grátia.
Hic ímpetrent fidélium
Voces precésque súpplicum
Domus beátæ múnera,
Partísque donis gáudeant:
Donec, solúti córpore,
Sedes beátas ímpleant.
Decus Parénti débitum
Sit usquequáque Altíssimo,
Natóque Patris único,
Et ínclito Paráclito,
Cui laus, potéstas, glória
Ætérna sit per sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_matutinum.lat:
Cæléstis urbs Jerúsalem,
Beáta pacis vísio,
Quæ celsa de vivéntibus
Saxis ad astra tólleris,
Sponsǽque ritu cíngeris
Mille Angelórum míllibus.
O sorte nupta próspera,
Dotáta Patris glória,
Respérsa Sponsi grátia,
Regína formosíssima,
Christo jugáta Príncipi,
Cæli corúsca cívitas.
Hic margarítis émicant,
Paténtque cunctis óstia;
Virtúte namque prǽvia
Mortális illuc dúcitur,
Amóre Christi pércitus
Torménta quisquis sústinet.
Scalpri salúbris íctibus
Et tunsióne plúrima,
Fabri políta málleo
Hanc saxa molem cónstruunt,
Aptísque juncta néxibus
Locántur in fastígio.
Decus Parénti débitum
Sit usquequáque Altíssimo,
Natóque Patris único,
Et ínclito Paráclito,
Cui laus, potéstas, glória
Ætérna sit per sǽcula.
Amen.

hymnus_vespera.eng:
Thou heavenly, new Jerusalem,
Vision of peace in prophet's dream!
With living stones built up on high,
And rising to yon starry sky;
In bridal pomp thy form is crowned,
With thousand thousand angels round!
O bride, betrothed in happy hour,
The Father's glory is thy dower;
The bridegroom's grace is shed on thee
Thou queen all fair eternally;
To Christ allied, thy Prince adored,
Bright shining city of the Lord!
Behold with pearls they glittering stand
thy peaceful gates to all expand;
By grace and strength divinely shed
Each mortal thither may be led;
Who, kindled by Christ's love, will dare
All earthly sufferings now to bear.
By many a salutary stroke,
By many a weary blow that broke,
Or polished with a workman's skill,
The stones that form that glorious pile,
They all are fitly framed to lie
In their appointed place on high.
Fair and well pleasing in thy sight,
Parent most high, enthroned in light,
And for thine only Son most meet,
And thee, all-glorious Paraclete,
To whom praise, power, and glory rise
Forever through the eternal skies.
Amen.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.lat: Tóllite portas, * príncipes vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles.
ant_1.eng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, * and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Non est hic áliud, * nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.
ant_2.eng: This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Qui hábitat * in adjutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
ant_3.eng: He that dwelleth in the help of the Most High * shall abide under the shadow of the God of heaven.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tóllite portas, * príncipes vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, * and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Erit mihi Dóminus * in Deum, et lapis iste vocábitur domus Dei.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord shall be my God, * and this stone shall be called God's house.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Moses built an altar * to the Lord God.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Non est hic áliud, * nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm4.eng: This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vidit Jacob scalam, * súmmitas ejus cælos tangébat, et descendéntes Angelos, et dixit: Vere locus iste sanctus est.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Jacob beheld a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and the angels of God descending on it. And he said: Surely this place is holy.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.lat: Eréxit Jacob * lápidem in títulum, fundens óleum désuper.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm6.eng: Jacob set up the stone for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.lat: Qui hábitat * in adjutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm7.eng: He that dwelleth in the help of the Most High * shall abide under the shadow of the God of heaven.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.lat: Templum Dómini * sanctum est, Dei structúra est, Dei ædificátio est.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm8.eng: The Temple of the Lord is holy. * The same is God's workmanship and God's building.

matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.lat: Benedícta * glória Dómini, de loco sancto suo, allelúja.
matutinum.antiphon.psalm9.eng: Blessed be the glory of the Lord * from His holy place. Alleluia.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 23

verses.lat: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo ejus: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
verses.eng: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

verses.lat: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
verses.eng: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

verses.lat: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?
verses.eng: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

verses.lat: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo.
verses.eng: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

verses.lat: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
verses.eng: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

verses.lat: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Jacob.
verses.eng: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:8 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus fortis et potens: Dóminus potens in prǽlio.
verses.eng: 23:8 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.

verses.lat: 23:9 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:9 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

verses.lat: 23:10 Quis est iste Rex glóriæ? * Dóminus virtútum ipse est Rex glóriæ.
verses.eng: 23:10 Who is this King of Glory? * the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Tóllite portas, * príncipes vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, * and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 45

verses.lat: 45:2 Deus noster refúgium, et virtus: * adjútor in tribulatiónibus, quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: 45:2 Our God is our refuge and strength: * a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: 45:3 Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra: * et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: 45:3 Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; * and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: 45:4 Sonuérunt, et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum: * conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled: * the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: 45:5 Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei: * sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: 45:5 The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: * the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.

verses.lat: 45:6 Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur: * adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: 45:6 God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: * God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: 45:7 Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna: * dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: 45:7 Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: * he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: 45:8 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:8 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: 45:9 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram: * áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ.
verses.eng: 45:9 Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth, * making wars to cease even to the end of the earth.

verses.lat: 45:10 Arcum cónteret, et confrínget arma: * et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: 45:10 He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: * and the shield he shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: 45:11 Vacáte, et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus: * exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: 45:11 Be still and see that I am God; * I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: 45:12 Dóminus virtútum nobíscum: * suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 45:12 The Lord of armies is with us: * the God of Jacob is our protector.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Erit mihi Dóminus * in Deum, et lapis iste vocábitur domus Dei.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: The Lord shall be my God, * and this stone shall be called God's house.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 47

verses.lat: 47:2 Magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis * in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 47:2 Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised * in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

verses.lat: 47:3 Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, * látera Aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
verses.eng: 47:3 With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, * on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.

verses.lat: 47:4 Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur: * cum suscípiet eam.
verses.eng: 47:4 In her houses shall God be known, * when he shall protect her.

verses.lat: 47:5 Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt: * convenérunt in unum.
verses.eng: 47:5 For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: * they gathered together.

verses.lat: 47:6 Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt: * tremor apprehéndit eos.
verses.eng: 47:6 So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: * trembling took hold of them.

verses.lat: 47:7 Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis: * in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
verses.eng: 47:7 There were pains as of a woman in labour; * with a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

verses.lat: 47:9 Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri: * Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 47:9 As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: * God hath founded it for ever.

verses.lat: 47:10 Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam, * in médio templi tui.
verses.eng: 47:10 We have received thy mercy, O God, * in the midst of thy temple.

verses.lat: 47:11 Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ: * justítia plena est déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 47:11 According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: * thy right hand is full of justice.

verses.lat: 47:12 Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ: * propter judícia tua, Dómine.
verses.eng: 47:12 Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: 47:13 Circúmdate Sion, et complectímini eam: * narráte in túrribus ejus.
verses.eng: 47:13 Surround Sion, and encompass her: * tell ye in her towers.

verses.lat: 47:14 Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus: * et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
verses.eng: 47:14 Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, * that ye may relate it in another generation.

verses.lat: 47:15 Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi: * ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
verses.eng: 47:15 For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: * he shall rule us for evermore.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Moses built an altar * to the Lord God.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 83

verses.lat: 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
verses.eng: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

verses.lat: 83:3 Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
verses.eng: 83:3 My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.

verses.lat: 83:4 Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
verses.eng: 83:4 For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:

verses.lat: 83:4 Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

verses.lat: 83:5 Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
verses.eng: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 83:6 Beátus vir, cujus est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.
verses.eng: 83:6 Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.

verses.lat: 83:8 Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.
verses.eng: 83:8 For the lawgiver shall give a blessing, they shall go from virtue to virtue: * the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.

verses.lat: 83:9 Dómine, Deus virtútum, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe, Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: 83:9 O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: * give ear, O God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 83:10 Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:
verses.eng: 83:10 Behold, O God our protector: * and look on the face of thy Christ.

verses.lat: 83:11 Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.
verses.eng: 83:11 For better is one day in thy courts * above thousands.

verses.lat: 83:11 Elégi abjéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
verses.eng: 83:11 I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.

verses.lat: 83:12 Quia misericórdiam, et veritátem díligit Deus: * grátiam et glóriam dabit Dóminus.
verses.eng: 83:12 For God loveth mercy and truth: * the Lord will give grace and glory.

verses.lat: 83:13 Non privábit bonis eos, qui ámbulant in innocéntia: * Dómine virtútum, beátus homo, qui sperat in te.
verses.eng: 83:13 He will not deprive of good things them that walk in innocence: * O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: Non est hic áliud, * nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 86

verses.lat: 86:1 Fundaménta ejus in móntibus sanctis: * díligit Dóminus portas Sion super ómnia tabernácula Jacob.
verses.eng: 86:1 The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains: * The Lord loveth the gates of Sion above all the tabernacles of Jacob.

verses.lat: 86:3 Gloriósa dicta sunt de te, * cívitas Dei.
verses.eng: 86:3 Glorious things are said of thee, * O city of God.

verses.lat: 86:4 Memor ero Rahab, et Babylónis * sciéntium me.
verses.eng: 86:4 I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon * knowing me.

verses.lat: 86:4 Ecce, alienígenæ, et Tyrus, et pópulus Æthíopum, * hi fuérunt illic.
verses.eng: 86:4 Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, * these were there.

verses.lat: 86:5 Numquid Sion dicet: Homo, et homo natus est in ea: * et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus?
verses.eng: 86:5 Shall not Sion say: This man and that man is born in her? * and the Highest himself hath founded her.

verses.lat: 86:6 Dóminus narrábit in scriptúris populórum, et príncipum: * horum, qui fuérunt in ea.
verses.eng: 86:6 The Lord shall tell in his writings of peoples and of princes, * of them that have been in her.

verses.lat: 86:7 Sicut lætántium ómnium * habitátio est in te.
verses.eng: 86:7 The dwelling in thee * is as it were of all rejoicing.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Vidit Jacob scalam, * súmmitas ejus cælos tangébat, et descendéntes Angelos, et dixit: Vere locus iste sanctus est.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: Jacob beheld a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven, and the angels of God descending on it. And he said: Surely this place is holy.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 87

verses.lat: 87:2 Dómine, Deus salútis meæ: * in die clamávi, et nocte coram te.
verses.eng: 87:2 Lord, the God of my salvation: * I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.

verses.lat: 87:3 Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:
verses.eng: 87:3 Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.

verses.lat: 87:4 Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
verses.eng: 87:4 For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

verses.lat: 87:5 Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adjutório, inter mórtuos liber.
verses.eng: 87:5 I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

verses.lat: 87:6 Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
verses.eng: 87:6 Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.

verses.lat: 87:7 Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
verses.eng: 87:7 They have laid me in the lower pit: * in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

verses.lat: 87:8 Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
verses.eng: 87:8 Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

verses.lat: 87:9 Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
verses.eng: 87:9 Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.

verses.lat: 87:9 Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
verses.eng: 87:9 I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.

verses.lat: 87:10 Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.
verses.eng: 87:10 All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: * I stretched out my hands to thee.

verses.lat: 87:11 Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
verses.eng: 87:11 Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

verses.lat: 87:12 Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
verses.eng: 87:12 Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?

verses.lat: 87:13 Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et justítia tua in terra obliviónis?
verses.eng: 87:13 Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

verses.lat: 87:14 Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
verses.eng: 87:14 But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: * and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

verses.lat: 87:15 Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
verses.eng: 87:15 Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?

verses.lat: 87:16 Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a juventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
verses.eng: 87:16 I am poor, and in labours from my youth: * and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

verses.lat: 87:17 In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
verses.eng: 87:17 Thy wrath hath come upon me: * and thy terrors have troubled me.

verses.lat: 87:18 Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.
verses.eng: 87:18 They have come round about me like water all the day: * they have compassed me about together.

verses.lat: 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.
verses.eng: 87:19 Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: * and my acquaintance, because of misery.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Eréxit Jacob * lápidem in títulum, fundens óleum désuper.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: Jacob set up the stone for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 90

verses.lat: 90:1 Qui hábitat in adjutório Altíssimi, * in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
verses.eng: 90:1 He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, * shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 90:2 Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
verses.eng: 90:2 He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: * my God, in him will I trust.

verses.lat: 90:3 Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
verses.eng: 90:3 For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: * and from the sharp word.

verses.lat: 90:4 Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis ejus sperábis.
verses.eng: 90:4 He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: * and under his wings thou shalt trust.

verses.lat: 90:5 Scuto circúmdabit te véritas ejus: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno,
verses.eng: 90:5 His truth shall compass thee with a shield: * thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.

verses.lat: 90:6 A sagítta volánte in die, † a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu, et dæmónio meridiáno.
verses.eng: 90:6 Of the arrow that flieth in the day, † of the business that walketh about in the dark: * of invasion, or of the noonday devil.

verses.lat: 90:7 Cadent a látere tuo mille, † et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
verses.eng: 90:7 A thousand shall fall at thy side, † and ten thousand at thy right hand: * but it shall not come nigh thee.

verses.lat: 90:8 Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
verses.eng: 90:8 But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: * and shalt see the reward of the wicked.

verses.lat: 90:9 Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
verses.eng: 90:9 Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: * thou hast made the most High thy refuge.

verses.lat: 90:10 Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
verses.eng: 90:10 There shall no evil come to thee: * nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.

verses.lat: 90:11 Quóniam Ángelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
verses.eng: 90:11 For he hath given his angels charge over thee; * to keep thee in all thy ways.

verses.lat: 90:12 In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
verses.eng: 90:12 In their hands they shall bear thee up: * lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

verses.lat: 90:13 Super áspidem, et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
verses.eng: 90:13 Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.

verses.lat: 90:14 Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum, quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
verses.eng: 90:14 Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he hath known my name.

verses.lat: 90:15 Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: ‡ cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: * erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
verses.eng: 90:15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: ‡ I am with him in tribulation, * I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.

verses.lat: 90:16 Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.
verses.eng: 90:16 I will fill him with length of days; * and I will shew him my salvation.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Qui hábitat * in adjutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: He that dwelleth in the help of the Most High * shall abide under the shadow of the God of heaven.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 95

verses.lat: 95:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * cantáte Dómino, omnis terra.
verses.eng: 95:1 Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: * sing to the Lord, all the earth.

verses.lat: 95:2 Cantáte Dómino, et benedícite nómini ejus: * annuntiáte de die in diem salutáre ejus.
verses.eng: 95:2 Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: * shew forth his salvation from day to day.

verses.lat: 95:3 Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus, * in ómnibus pópulis mirabília ejus.
verses.eng: 95:3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles: * his wonders among all people.

verses.lat: 95:4 Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 95:4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: * he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.lat: 95:5 Quóniam omnes dii géntium dæmónia: * Dóminus autem cælos fecit.
verses.eng: 95:5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: * but the Lord made the heavens.

verses.lat: 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo in conspéctu ejus: * sanctimónia et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne ejus.
verses.eng: 95:6 Praise and beauty are before him: * holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.

verses.lat: 95:7 Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
verses.eng: 95:7 Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour: * bring to the Lord glory unto his name.

verses.lat: 95:8 Tóllite hóstias, et introíte in átria ejus: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 95:8 Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

verses.lat: 95:9 Commoveátur a fácie ejus univérsa terra: * dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit.
verses.eng: 95:9 Let all the earth be moved at his presence. * Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned.

verses.lat: 95:10 Étenim corréxit orbem terræ qui non commovébitur: * judicábit pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 95:10 For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: * he will judge the people with justice.

verses.lat: 95:11 Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra: commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: * gaudébunt campi, et ómnia quæ in eis sunt.
verses.eng: 95:11 Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fulness thereof: * the fields and all things that are in them shall be joyful.

verses.lat: 95:12 Tunc exsultábunt ómnia ligna silvárum a fácie Dómini, quia venit: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 95:12 Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice before the face of the Lord, because he cometh: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, * et pópulos in veritáte sua.
verses.eng: 95:13 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with his truth.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Templum Dómini * sanctum est, Dei structúra est, Dei ædificátio est.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: The Temple of the Lord is holy. * The same is God's workmanship and God's building.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 98

verses.lat: 98:1 Dóminus regnávit, irascántur pópuli: * qui sedet super Chérubim, moveátur terra.
verses.eng: 98:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry: * he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved.

verses.lat: 98:2 Dóminus in Sion magnus: * et excélsus super omnes pópulos.
verses.eng: 98:2 The Lord is great in Sion, * and high above all people.

verses.lat: 98:3 Confiteántur nómini tuo magno: quóniam terríbile, et sanctum est: * et honor regis judícium díligit.
verses.eng: 98:3 Let them give praise to thy great name: for it is terrible and holy: * and the king’s honour loveth judgment.

verses.lat: 98:4 Tu parásti directiónes: * judícium et justítiam in Jacob tu fecísti.
verses.eng: 98:4 Thou hast prepared directions: * thou hast done judgment and justice in Jacob.

verses.lat: 98:5 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte scabéllum pedum ejus: * quóniam sanctum est.
verses.eng: 98:5 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore his footstool, * for it is holy.

verses.lat: 98:6 Móyses et Aaron in sacerdótibus ejus: * et Sámuel inter eos, qui ínvocant nomen ejus:
verses.eng: 98:6 Moses and Aaron among his priests: * and Samuel among them that call upon his name.

verses.lat: 98:6 Invocábant Dóminum, et ipse exaudiébat eos: * in colúmna nubis loquebátur ad eos.
verses.eng: 98:6 They called upon the Lord, and he heard them: * he spoke to them in the pillar of the cloud.

verses.lat: 98:7 Custodiébant testimónia ejus, * et præcéptum quod dedit illis.
verses.eng: 98:7 They kept his testimonies, * and the commandment which he gave them.

verses.lat: 98:8 Dómine, Deus noster, tu exaudiébas eos: * Deus, tu propítius fuísti eis, et ulcíscens in omnes adinventiónes eórum.
verses.eng: 98:8 Thou didst hear them, O Lord our God: * thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions.

verses.lat: 98:9 Exaltáte Dóminum, Deum nostrum, et adoráte in monte sancto ejus: * quóniam sanctus Dóminus, Deus noster.
verses.eng: 98:9 Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore at his holy mountain: * for the Lord our God is holy.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Benedícta * glória Dómini, de loco sancto suo, allelúja.
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: Blessed be the glory of the Lord * from His holy place. Alleluia.

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: Tóllite portas, * príncipes vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, * and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: Non est hic áliud, * nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: This is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Qui hábitat * in adjutório Altíssimi, in protectióne Dei cæli commorábitur.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: He that dwelleth in the help of the Most High * shall abide under the shadow of the God of heaven.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 109

verses.lat: 109:1a Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
verses.eng: 109:1a The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

verses.lat: 109:1b Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:1b Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

verses.lat: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

verses.lat: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
verses.eng: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

verses.lat: 109:4 Jurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
verses.eng: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

verses.lat: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
verses.eng: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

verses.lat: 109:6 Judicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
verses.eng: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

verses.lat: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
verses.eng: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonLat: Domum tuam, Dómine, * decet sanctitúdo in longitúdinem diérum.
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Holiness becometh thine house, * O Lord, for ever.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 110

verses.lat: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio justórum, et congregatióne.
verses.eng: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

verses.lat: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes ejus.
verses.eng: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

verses.lat: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus ejus: * et justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, † miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * (5a) escam dedit timéntibus se.
verses.eng: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, † being a merciful and gracious Lord: * (5a) he hath given food to them that fear him.

verses.lat: 110:5b Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * (6) virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
verses.eng: 110:5b He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * (6) he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

verses.lat: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum ejus véritas, et judícium.
verses.eng: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

verses.lat: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta ejus: † confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
verses.eng: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: † confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

verses.lat: 110:9a Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
verses.eng: 110:9a He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

verses.lat: 110:9b (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen ejus: * (10a) inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
verses.eng: 110:9b (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * (10a) the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

verses.lat: 110:10b Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 110:10b A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: My house * shall be called the house of prayer.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 111

verses.lat: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis ejus volet nimis.
verses.eng: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

verses.lat: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen ejus: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
verses.eng: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

verses.lat: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo ejus: * et justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et justus.
verses.eng: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

verses.lat: 111:5 Jucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, † dispónet sermónes suos in judício: * (6) quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
verses.eng: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: † he shall order his words with judgment: * (6) because he shall not be moved for ever.

verses.lat: 111:7a In memória ætérna erit justus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
verses.eng: 111:7a The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

verses.lat: 111:7b Parátum cor ejus speráre in Dómino, † (8) confirmátum est cor ejus: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
verses.eng: 111:7b His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: † (8) his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

verses.lat: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: † justítia ejus manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu ejus exaltábitur in glória.
verses.eng: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: † his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

verses.lat: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, † déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
verses.eng: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, † he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Hæc est domus Dómini * fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: This is the Lord's house * stoutly builded, well founded upon a sure rock.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 112

verses.lat: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
verses.eng: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

verses.lat: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória ejus.
verses.eng: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

verses.lat: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * (6) et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
verses.eng: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * (6) and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

verses.lat: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
verses.eng: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

verses.lat: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
verses.eng: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

verses.lat: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
verses.eng: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Bene fundáta est * domus Dómini supra firmam petram.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: The Lord's house is well founded * upon a sure rock.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 147

verses.lat: 147:1 Lauda, Jerúsalem, Dóminum: * lauda Deum tuum, Sion.
verses.eng: 147:1 Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: * praise thy God, O Sion.

verses.lat: 147:2 Quóniam confortávit seras portárum tuárum: * benedíxit fíliis tuis in te.
verses.eng: 147:2 Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates * he hath blessed thy children within thee.

verses.lat: 147:3 Qui pósuit fines tuos pacem: * et ádipe fruménti sátiat te.
verses.eng: 147:3 Who hath placed peace in thy borders: * and filleth thee with the fat of corn.

verses.lat: 147:4 Qui emíttit elóquium suum terræ: * velóciter currit sermo ejus.
verses.eng: 147:4 Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: * his word runneth swiftly.

verses.lat: 147:5 Qui dat nivem sicut lanam: * nébulam sicut cínerem spargit.
verses.eng: 147:5 Who giveth snow like wool: * scattereth mists like ashes.

verses.lat: 147:6 Mittit crystállum suam sicut buccéllas: * ante fáciem frígoris ejus quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 147:6 He sendeth his crystal like morsels: * who shall stand before the face of his cold?

verses.lat: 147:7 Emíttet verbum suum, et liquefáciet ea: * flabit spíritus ejus, et fluent aquæ.
verses.eng: 147:7 He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: * his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.

verses.lat: 147:8 Qui annúntiat verbum suum Jacob: * justítias, et judícia sua Israël.
verses.eng: 147:8 Who declareth his word to Jacob: * his justices and his judgments to Israel.

verses.lat: 147:9 Non fecit táliter omni natióni: * et judícia sua non manifestávit eis.
verses.eng: 147:9 He hath not done in like manner to every nation: * and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them.

vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Lápides pretiósi * omnes muri tui, et turres Jerúsalem gemmis ædificabúntur.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: All thy walls are of stones most precious, * and the towers of Jerusalem shall be built up with jewels.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. In dedicatióne templi decantábat pópulus laudem: 
* Et in ore eórum dulcis resonábat sonus.
V. Fundáta est domus Dómini supra vérticem móntium, et vénient ad eam omnes gentes.
R. Et in ore eórum dulcis resonábat sonus.
responsory1.eng:
R. When the Temple was dedicated the people sang praise;
* And sweet in their mouths was the sound.
V. The Lord's house is established in the top of the mountains; and all nations shall flow unto it.
R. And sweet in their mouths was the sound.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Fundáta est domus Dómini supra vérticem móntium, et exaltáta est super omnes colles:
* Et vénient ad eam omnes gentes, et dicent: Glória tibi, Dómine.
V. Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, portántes manípulos suos.
R. Et vénient ad eam omnes gentes, et dicent: Glória tibi, Dómine.
responsory2.eng:
R. The Lord's house is established in the top of the mountains, and exalted above the hills;
* And all nations shall flow unto it, and shall say: Glory be to thee, O Lord!
V. They shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing their sheaves with them.
R. And all nations shall flow unto it, and shall say: Glory be to thee, O Lord!

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Bénedic, Dómine, domum istam, quam ædificávi nómini tuo: veniéntium in loco isto 
* Exáudi preces in excélso sólio glóriæ tuæ.
V. Dómine, si convérsus fúerit pópulus tuus, et oráverit ad sanctuárium tuum.
R. Exáudi preces in excélso sólio glóriæ tuæ.
&Gloria
R. Exáudi preces in excélso sólio glóriæ tuæ.
responsory3.eng:
R. O Lord, bless this house which I have built unto thy name. whosoever shall come unto this place and pray, then
* Hear thou from the excellent throne of thy glory.
V. O Lord, if thy people turn and pray toward thy sanctuary.
R. Hear thou from the excellent throne of thy glory.
&Gloria
R. Hear Thou from the excellent throne of thy glory.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Orántibus in loco isto, 
* Dimítte peccáta pópuli tui, Deus, et osténde eis viam bonam per quam ámbulent, et da glóriam in loco isto.
V. Qui regis Israël inténde, qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph, qui sedes super Chérubim.
R. Dimítte peccáta pópuli tui, Deus, et osténde eis viam bonam per quam ámbulent, et da glóriam in loco isto.
responsory4.eng:
R. If they pray toward this place,
* Forgive the sin of thy people, O God, and teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and manifest forth thy glory in this place.
V. Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock, thou that sittest upon the cherubim.
R. Forgive the sin of thy people, O God, and teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and manifest forth thy glory in this place.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. O quam metuéndus est locus iste: 
* Vere non est hic áliud nisi domus Dei et porta cæli.
V. Hæc est domus Dómini fírmiter ædificáta, bene fundáta est supra firmam petram.
R. Vere non est hic áliud nisi domus Dei et porta cæli.
responsory5.eng:
R. How dreadful is this place!
* Surely this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
V. This is the house of God, stoutly builded, well founded upon a sure rock.
R. Surely this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Mane surgens Jacob, erigébat lápidem in títulum, fundens óleum désuper; votum vovit Dómino: 
* Vere locus iste sanctus est, et ego nesciébam.
V. Cumque evigilásset Jacob de somno, ait.
R. Vere locus iste sanctus est, et ego nesciébam.
&Gloria
R. Vere locus iste sanctus est, et ego nesciébam.
responsory6.eng:
R. Jacob rose up early in the morning, and set up the stone for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it, and vowed a vow unto the Lord.
* Surely this place is holy, and I knew it not.
V. And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said
R. Surely this place is holy, and I knew it not.
&Gloria
R. Surely this place is holy, and I knew it not.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Domus mea, domus oratiónis vocábitur, dicit Dóminus: in ea omnis qui petit, áccipit; et qui quærit, ínvenit; 
* Et pulsánti aperiétur.
V. Pétite, et accipiétis; quǽrite, et inveniétis.
R. Et pulsánti aperiétur.
responsory7.eng:
R. My house shall be called the house of prayer, saith the Lord. Therein, he that asketh, receiveth; he that seeketh, findeth;
* And to him that knocketh, it shall be opened.
V. Ask, and ye shall receive; seek, and ye shall find.
R. And to him that knocketh, it shall be opened.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Lápides pretiósi omnes muri tui, 
* Et turres Jerúsalem gemmis ædificabúntur.
V. Portæ Jerúsalem ex sapphíro et smarágdo ædificabúntur, et ex lápide pretióso omnis circúitus muri ejus.
R. Et turres Jerúsalem gemmis ædificabúntur.
&Gloria
R. Et turres Jerúsalem gemmis ædificabúntur.
responsory8.eng:
R. All thy walls are of stones most precious.
* The towers of Jerusalem shall be built up with jewels.
V. The gates of Jerusalem shall be built up with the sapphire stone, and the emerald, and all her walls round about with stones most precious.
R. The towers of Jerusalem shall be built up with jewels.
&Gloria
R. The towers of Jerusalem shall be built up with jewels.

ant_laudes.eng: I am the resurrection and the life: * he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live; and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.
ant_laudes.lat: Ego sum * resurréctio et vita: qui credit in me, étiam si mórtuus fúerit, vivet; et omnis qui vivit et credit in me, non moriétur in ætérnum.

ant_vespera.eng: All that the Father giveth Me shall come to Me; * and him that cometh to Me I will in no wise cast out.
ant_vespera.lat: Omne * quod dat mihi Pater, ad me véniet; et eum qui venit ad me, non eíciam foras.

invit.eng: Unto the Eternal King all live. * O come, let us worship Him.
invit.lat: Regem, cui ómnia vivunt, * Veníte adorémus.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: The bones which thou hast broken * may rejoice.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Exsultábunt Dómino * ossa humiliáta.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Lord, hear * my prayer; unto thee shall all flesh come.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Exáudi, Dómine, * oratiónem meam: ad te omnis caro véniet.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thy right hand * upholdeth me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: From the gates of hell * deliver my soul, O Lord.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: A porta ínferi * érue, Dómine, ánimam meam.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Let everything that hath breath * praise the Lord.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Omnis spíritus * laudet Dóminum.

versum_1.eng:
V. I heard a voice from heaven, saying unto me:
R. Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord.
versum_1.lat:
V. Audívi vocem de cælo dicéntem mihi.
R. Beáti mórtui qui in Dómino moriúntur.

versum_2.eng:
V. I heard a voice from heaven, saying unto me:
R. Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord.
versum_2.lat:
V. Audívi vocem de cælo dicéntem mihi.
R. Beáti mórtui qui in Dómino moriúntur.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: I will walk before the Lord * in the land of the living.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Placébo Dómino * in regióne vivórum.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Woe is me! O Lord, * that my sojourn is long
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Heu mihi Dómine, * quia incolátus meus prolongátus est.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Lord shall keep thee from all evil, * the Lord shall keep thy soul.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: If Thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, * O Lord, who shall stand.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Si iniquitátes * observáveris, Dómine: Dómine, quis sustinébit?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: O Lord, forsake not * the works of thine own hands.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Opera * mánuum tuárum, Dómine, ne despícias.

matutinum.psalm2.label: Psalmus 5

verses.lat: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
verses.eng: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

verses.lat: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

verses.lat: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
verses.eng: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

verses.lat: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
verses.eng: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

verses.lat: 5:6 Neque habitábit juxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt injústi ante óculos tuos.
verses.eng: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

verses.lat: 5:7a Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
verses.eng: 5:7a Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

verses.lat: 5:7b Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * (8a) ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 5:7b The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * (8a) But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

verses.lat: 5:8b Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
verses.eng: 5:8b I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

verses.lat: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in justítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
verses.eng: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

verses.lat: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
verses.eng: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

verses.lat: 5:11a Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, † linguis suis dolóse agébant, * júdica illos, Deus.
verses.eng: 5:11a Their throat is an open sepulchre: † they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

verses.lat: 5:11b Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, † secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 5:11b Let them fall from their devices: † according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 5:12a Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
verses.eng: 5:12a But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

verses.lat: 5:12b Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * (13a) quóniam tu benedíces justo.
verses.eng: 5:12b And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * (13a) For thou wilt bless the just.

verses.lat: 5:13b Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
verses.eng: 5:13b O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.

matutinum.psalm2.antiphonLat: Dírige, * Dómine, Deus meus, in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
matutinum.psalm2.antiphonEng: Make my way straight before thy face, * O Lord my God.

matutinum.psalm3.label: Psalmus 6

verses.lat: 6:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
verses.eng: 6:2 Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

verses.lat: 6:3 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
verses.eng: 6:3 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.

verses.lat: 6:4 Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
verses.eng: 6:4 And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?

verses.lat: 6:5 Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
verses.eng: 6:5 Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.

verses.lat: 6:6 Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
verses.eng: 6:6 For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?

verses.lat: 6:7 Laborávi in gémitu meo, † lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
verses.eng: 6:7 I have laboured in my groanings, † every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.

verses.lat: 6:8 Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
verses.eng: 6:8 My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.

verses.lat: 6:9 Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
verses.eng: 6:9 Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.

verses.lat: 6:10 Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
verses.eng: 6:10 The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.

verses.lat: 6:11 Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
verses.eng: 6:11 Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.

matutinum.psalm3.antiphonLat: Convértere, * Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: quóniam non est in morte, qui memor sit tui.
matutinum.psalm3.antiphonEng: Return, O Lord, deliver my soul * O save me for thy mercy's sake.

matutinum.psalm4.label: Psalmus 7

verses.lat: 7:2 Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
verses.eng: 7:2 O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.

verses.lat: 7:3 Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
verses.eng: 7:3 Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.

verses.lat: 7:4 Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
verses.eng: 7:4 O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:

verses.lat: 7:5 Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
verses.eng: 7:5 If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.

verses.lat: 7:6 Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, † et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
verses.eng: 7:6 Let the enemy pursue my soul, † and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.

verses.lat: 7:7a Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
verses.eng: 7:7a Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.

verses.lat: 7:7b Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * (8a) et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
verses.eng: 7:7b And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * (8a) and a congregation of people shall surround thee.

verses.lat: 7:8b Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * (9a) Dóminus júdicat pópulos.
verses.eng: 7:8b And for their sakes return thou on high. * (9a) The Lord judgeth the people.

verses.lat: 7:9b Júdica me, Dómine, secúndum justítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
verses.eng: 7:9b Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.

verses.lat: 7:10 Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges justum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
verses.eng: 7:10 The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.

verses.lat: 7:11 Justum adjutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
verses.eng: 7:11 Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.

verses.lat: 7:12 Deus judex justus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
verses.eng: 7:12 God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?

verses.lat: 7:13 Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
verses.eng: 7:13 Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

verses.lat: 7:14 Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
verses.eng: 7:14 And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.

verses.lat: 7:15 Ecce, partúriit injustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
verses.eng: 7:15 Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.

verses.lat: 7:16 Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
verses.eng: 7:16 He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.

verses.lat: 7:17 Convertétur dolor ejus in caput ejus: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas ejus descéndet.
verses.eng: 7:17 His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.

verses.lat: 7:18 Confitébor Dómino secúndum justítiam ejus: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
verses.eng: 7:18 I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.

matutinum.psalm4.antiphonLat: Nequándo rápiat * ut leo ánimam meam, dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
matutinum.psalm4.antiphonEng: Lest he tear my soul like a lion, * while there is none to deliver, or to save.

matutinum.psalm5.label: Psalmus 22

verses.lat: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
verses.eng: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

verses.lat: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
verses.eng: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

verses.lat: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas justítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
verses.eng: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

verses.lat: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
verses.eng: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

verses.lat: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
verses.eng: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

verses.lat: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
verses.eng: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

verses.lat: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
verses.eng: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

verses.lat: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

verses.lat: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
verses.eng: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

matutinum.psalm5.antiphonLat: In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit.
matutinum.psalm5.antiphonEng: He maketh me to lie down * in green pastures.

matutinum.psalm6.label: Psalmus 24

verses.lat: 24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
verses.eng: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

verses.lat: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
verses.eng: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

verses.lat: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
verses.eng: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

verses.lat: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
verses.eng: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

verses.lat: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
verses.eng: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

verses.lat: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
verses.eng: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

verses.lat: 24:7 Delícta juventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
verses.eng: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

verses.lat: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
verses.eng: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

verses.lat: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
verses.eng: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

verses.lat: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in judício: * docébit mites vias suas.
verses.eng: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

verses.lat: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum ejus et testimónia ejus.
verses.eng: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

verses.lat: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
verses.eng: 24:11 For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

verses.lat: 24:12 Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
verses.eng: 24:12 Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

verses.lat: 24:13 Ánima ejus in bonis demorábitur: * et semen ejus hereditábit terram.
verses.eng: 24:13 His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

verses.lat: 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
verses.eng: 24:14 The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

verses.lat: 24:15 Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
verses.eng: 24:15 My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

verses.lat: 24:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
verses.eng: 24:16 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

verses.lat: 24:17 Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
verses.eng: 24:17 The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

verses.lat: 24:18 Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
verses.eng: 24:18 See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

verses.lat: 24:19 Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
verses.eng: 24:19 Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

verses.lat: 24:20 Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
verses.eng: 24:20 Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

verses.lat: 24:21 Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
verses.eng: 24:21 The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

verses.lat: 24:22 Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
verses.eng: 24:22 Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

matutinum.psalm6.antiphonLat: Delícta * juventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.
matutinum.psalm6.antiphonEng: Lord, remember not the sins of my youth, * nor my transgressions.

matutinum.psalm7.label: Psalmus 26

verses.lat: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
verses.eng: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

verses.lat: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
verses.eng: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

verses.lat: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
verses.eng: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

verses.lat: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
verses.eng: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

verses.lat: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
verses.eng: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

verses.lat: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
verses.eng: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

verses.lat: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
verses.eng: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

verses.lat: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum ejus.
verses.eng: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

verses.lat: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
verses.eng: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

verses.lat: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
verses.eng: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

verses.lat: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo ejus hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
verses.eng: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

verses.lat: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

verses.lat: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
verses.eng: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

verses.lat: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
verses.eng: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

verses.lat: 26:9 Adjútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
verses.eng: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

verses.lat: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
verses.eng: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

verses.lat: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
verses.eng: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

verses.lat: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
verses.eng: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

verses.lat: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

verses.lat: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
verses.eng: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

matutinum.psalm7.antiphonLat: Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
matutinum.psalm7.antiphonEng: I believe that I shall yet see the goodness of the Lord * in the land of the living.

matutinum.psalm8.label: Psalmus 39

verses.lat: 39:2 Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, * et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: 39:2 With expectation I have waited for the Lord, * and he was attentive to me.

verses.lat: 39:3 Et exaudívit preces meas: * et edúxit me de lacu misériæ, et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: 39:3 And he heard my prayers, * and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: 39:3 Et státuit super petram pedes meos: * et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: 39:3 And he set my feet upon a rock, * and directed my steps.

verses.lat: 39:4 Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, * carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: 39:4 And he put a new canticle into my mouth, * a song to our God.

verses.lat: 39:4 Vidébunt multi, et timébunt: * et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: 39:4 Many shall see, and shall fear: * and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: 39:5 Beátus vir, cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus: * et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: 39:5 Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; * and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.

verses.lat: 39:6 Multa fecísti tu, Dómine, Deus meus, mirabília tua: * et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: 39:6 Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: * and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee.

verses.lat: 39:6 Annuntiávi et locútus sum: * multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: 39:6 I have declared and I have spoken * they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: 39:7 Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti: * aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: 39:7 Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; * but thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: 39:7 Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti: * tunc dixi: Ecce, vénio.
verses.eng: 39:7 Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require: * then said I, Behold I come.

verses.lat: 39:8 In cápite libri scriptum est de me ut fácerem voluntátem tuam: * Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: 39:8 In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do thy will: * O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: 39:10 Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna, * ecce, lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: 39:10 I have declared thy justice in a great church, * lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.

verses.lat: 39:11 Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo: * veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: 39:11 I have not hid thy justice within my heart: * I have declared thy truth and thy salvation.

verses.lat: 39:11 Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam * a concílio multo.
verses.eng: 39:11 I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth * from a great council.

verses.lat: 39:12 Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me: * misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: 39:12 Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: * thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: 39:13 Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala, quorum non est númerus: * comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: 39:13 For evils without number have surrounded me; * my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: 39:13 Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: 39:13 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: * and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: 39:15 Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: 39:15 Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

verses.lat: 39:15 Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: 39:15 Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: 39:16 Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: 39:16 Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

verses.lat: 39:17 Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: 39:18 Adjútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

matutinum.psalm8.antiphonLat: Compláceat * tibi, Dómine, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
matutinum.psalm8.antiphonEng: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me * O Lord, look upon me to help me.

matutinum.psalm9.label: Psalmus 40

verses.lat: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
verses.eng: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
