verses.lat: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum ejus.
verses.eng: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

verses.lat: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris ejus: * univérsum stratum ejus versásti in infirmitáte ejus.
verses.eng: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

verses.lat: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
verses.eng: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

verses.lat: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen ejus?
verses.eng: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

verses.lat: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor ejus congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
verses.eng: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

verses.lat: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
verses.eng: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

verses.lat: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
verses.eng: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

verses.lat: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
verses.eng: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

verses.lat: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
verses.eng: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

verses.lat: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
verses.eng: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

verses.lat: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
verses.eng: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

verses.lat: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
verses.eng: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

verses.lat: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
verses.eng: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

matutinum.psalm9.antiphonLat: Sana, Dómine, * ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
matutinum.psalm9.antiphonEng: Lord, heal my soul; * for I have sinned against thee.

matutinum.psalm10.label: Psalmus 41

verses.lat: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
verses.eng: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

verses.lat: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
verses.eng: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

verses.lat: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
verses.eng: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

verses.lat: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
verses.eng: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

verses.lat: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
verses.eng: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

verses.lat: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

verses.lat: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Jordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
verses.eng: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

verses.lat: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
verses.eng: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

verses.lat: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
verses.eng: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

verses.lat: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum ejus.
verses.eng: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

verses.lat: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
verses.eng: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

verses.lat: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
verses.eng: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
verses.eng: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

verses.lat: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

matutinum.psalm10.antiphonLat: Sitívit * ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?
matutinum.psalm10.antiphonEng: My soul thirsteth for the living God; * when shall I come and appear before God?

matutinum.ant_1.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_1.lat: Dírige, * Dómine, Deus meus, in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
matutinum.ant_1.eng: Make my way straight before thy face, * O Lord my God.

matutinum.ant_2.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_2.lat: In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit.
matutinum.ant_2.eng: He maketh me to lie down * in green pastures.

matutinum.ant_3.label: Antíphona
matutinum.ant_3.lat: Compláceat * tibi, Dómine, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
matutinum.ant_3.eng: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me * O Lord, look upon me to help me.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 114

verses.lat: 114:1 Diléxi, quóniam exáudiet Dóminus * vocem oratiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 114:1 I have loved, because the Lord will hear * the voice of my prayer.

verses.lat: 114:2 Quia inclinávit aurem suam mihi: * et in diébus meis invocábo.
verses.eng: 114:2 Because he hath inclined his ear unto me: * and in my days I will call upon him.

verses.lat: 114:3a Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et perícula inférni invenérunt me.
verses.eng: 114:3a The sorrows of death have compassed me: * and the perils of hell have found me.

verses.lat: 114:3b Tribulatiónem et dolórem invéni: * (4a) et nomen Dómini invocávi.
verses.eng: 114:3b I met with trouble and sorrow: * (4a) and I called upon the name of the Lord.

verses.lat: 114:4b O Dómine, líbera ánimam meam: ‡ (5) miséricors Dóminus, et justus, * et Deus noster miserétur.
verses.eng: 114:4b O Lord, deliver my soul. ‡ (5) The Lord is merciful and just, * and our God sheweth mercy.

verses.lat: 114:6 Custódiens párvulos Dóminus: * humiliátus sum, et liberávit me.
verses.eng: 114:6 The Lord is the keeper of little ones: * I was humbled, and he delivered me.

verses.lat: 114:7 Convértere, ánima mea, in réquiem tuam: * quia Dóminus benefécit tibi.
verses.eng: 114:7 Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: * for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.

verses.lat: 114:8 Quia erípuit ánimam meam de morte: ‡ óculos meos a lácrimis, * pedes meos a lapsu.
verses.eng: 114:8 For he hath delivered my soul from death: ‡ my eyes from tears, * my feet from falling.

verses.lat: 114:9 Placébo Dómino * in regióne vivórum.
verses.eng: 114:9 I will please the Lord * in the land of the living.

vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: I will walk before the Lord * in the land of the living.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 119

verses.lat: 119:1 Ad Dóminum cum tribulárer clamávi: * et exaudívit me.
verses.eng: 119:1 In my trouble I cried to the Lord: * and he heard me.

verses.lat: 119:2 Dómine, líbera ánimam meam a lábiis iníquis, * et a lingua dolósa.
verses.eng: 119:2 O Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips, * and a deceitful tongue.

verses.lat: 119:3 Quid detur tibi, aut quid apponátur tibi * ad linguam dolósam?
verses.eng: 119:3 What shall be given to thee, or what shall be added to thee, * to a deceitful tongue?

verses.lat: 119:4 Sagíttæ poténtis acútæ, * cum carbónibus desolatóriis.
verses.eng: 119:4 The sharp arrows of the mighty, * with coals that lay waste.

verses.lat: 119:5 Heu mihi, quia incolátus meus prolongátus est: † habitávi cum habitántibus Cedar: * (6) multum íncola fuit ánima mea.
verses.eng: 119:5 Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged! † I have dwelt with the inhabitants of Cedar: * (6) my soul hath been long a sojourner.

verses.lat: 119:7 Cum his, qui odérunt pacem, eram pacíficus: * cum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
verses.eng: 119:7 With them that hated peace I was peaceable: * when I spoke to them they fought against me without cause.

vesperae.psalm2.antiphonLat: Heu mihi Dómine, * quia incolátus meus prolongátus est.
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Woe is me! O Lord, * that my sojourn is long

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 120

verses.lat: 120:1 Levávi óculos meos in montes, * unde véniet auxílium mihi.
verses.eng: 120:1 I have lifted up my eyes to the mountains, * from whence help shall come to me.

verses.lat: 120:2 Auxílium meum a Dómino, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
verses.eng: 120:2 My help is from the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.

verses.lat: 120:3 Non det in commotiónem pedem tuum: * neque dormítet qui custódit te.
verses.eng: 120:3 May he not suffer thy foot to be moved: * neither let him slumber that keepeth thee.

verses.lat: 120:4 Ecce, non dormitábit neque dórmiet, * qui custódit Israël.
verses.eng: 120:4 Behold he shall neither slumber nor sleep, * that keepeth Israel.

verses.lat: 120:5 Dóminus custódit te, Dóminus protéctio tua, * super manum déxteram tuam.
verses.eng: 120:5 The Lord is thy keeper, the Lord is thy protection * upon thy right hand.

verses.lat: 120:6 Per diem sol non uret te: * neque luna per noctem.
verses.eng: 120:6 The sun shall not burn thee by day: * nor the moon by night.

verses.lat: 120:7 Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.
verses.eng: 120:7 The Lord keepeth thee from all evil: * may the Lord keep thy soul.

verses.lat: 120:8 Dóminus custódiat intróitum tuum, et éxitum tuum: * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 120:8 May the Lord keep thy coming in and thy going out; * from henceforth now and for ever.

vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: Dóminus custódit te ab omni malo: * custódiat ánimam tuam Dóminus.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: The Lord shall keep thee from all evil, * the Lord shall keep thy soul.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 129

verses.lat: 129:1 De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
verses.eng: 129:1 Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.

verses.lat: 129:2 Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 129:2 Let thy ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: 129:3 Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 129:3 If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it.

verses.lat: 129:4 Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 129:4 For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: * and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 129:5 Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo ejus: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:5 My soul hath relied on his word: * my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:6 A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:6 From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:7 Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia: * et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
verses.eng: 129:7 Because with the Lord there is mercy: * and with him plentiful redemption.

verses.lat: 129:8 Et ipse rédimet Israël, * ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
verses.eng: 129:8 And he shall redeem Israel * from all his iniquities.

vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Si iniquitátes * observáveris, Dómine: Dómine, quis sustinébit?
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: If Thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, * O Lord, who shall stand.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 137

verses.lat: 137:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.
verses.eng: 137:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * for thou hast heard the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: 137:2 In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.
verses.eng: 137:2 I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the Angels: * I will worship towards thy holy temple, and I will give glory to thy name.

verses.lat: 137:3 Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.
verses.eng: 137:3 For thy mercy, and for thy truth: * for thou hast magnified thy holy name

verses.lat: 137:4 In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.
verses.eng: 137:4 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me: * thou shalt multiply strength in my soul.

verses.lat: 137:5 Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:
verses.eng: 137:5 May all the kings of the earth give glory to thee: * for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.

verses.lat: 137:6 Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.
verses.eng: 137:6 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: * for great is the glory of the Lord.

verses.lat: 137:7 Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.
verses.eng: 137:7 For the Lord is high, and looketh on the low: * and the high he knoweth afar off.

verses.lat: 137:8 Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.
verses.eng: 137:8 If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: * and thou hast stretched forth thy hand against the wrath of my enemies: and thy right hand hath saved me.

verses.lat: 137:9 Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.
verses.eng: 137:9 The Lord will repay for me: * thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: O despise not the works of thy hands.

vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Opera * mánuum tuárum, Dómine, ne despícias.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: O Lord, forsake not * the works of thine own hands.

responsory1.label: Responsorium
responsory1.lat:
R. Credo quod Redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum, 
* Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
V. Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et non álius; et óculi mei conspectúri sunt.
R. Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
responsory1.eng:
R. I believe that my Redeemer liveth, and that I shall stand up from the earth at the latter day,
* And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.
V. Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another.
R. And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.

responsory2.label: Responsorium
responsory2.lat:
R. Qui Lázarum resuscitásti a monuménto fœ́tidum, 
* Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
V. Qui ventúrus es judicáre vivos et mórtuos, et sǽculum per ignem.
R. Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
responsory2.eng:
R. Thou Who didst call up Lazarus from the grave after that he had begun to stink
* Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.
V. Thou Who shalt come to judge the quick and dead, and the world by fire
R. Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.

responsory3.label: Responsorium
responsory3.lat:
R. Dómine, quando véneris judicáre terram, ubi me abscóndam a vultu iræ tuæ? 
* Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
V. Commíssa mea pavésco, et ante te erubésco: dum véneris judicáre, noli me condemnáre.
R. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
$Requiem
R. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
responsory3.eng:
R. Lord, when Thou comest to judge the earth, where shall I hide myself from the face of thy wrath?
* For I have sinned greatly in my life.
V. I dread my sins, I blush before thee I see the great tribunal set! In fear and terror I implore thee, Forgive when soul and Judge are met!
R. For I have sinned greatly in my life.
$Requiem
R. For I have sinned greatly in my life.

responsory4.label: Responsorium
responsory4.lat:
R. Meménto mei, Deus, quia ventus est vita mea, 
* Nec aspíciat me visus hóminis.
V. De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: Dómine, exáudi vocem meam.
R. Nec aspíciat me visus hóminis.
responsory4.eng:
R. Remember, O God, that my life is wind.
* The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more.
V. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord! Lord, hear my voice.
R. The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more.

responsory5.label: Responsorium
responsory5.lat:
R. Hei mihi, Dómine, quia peccávi nimis in vita mea: Quid fáciam, miser? ubi fúgiam, nisi ad te, Deus meus? 
* Miserére mei, dum véneris in novíssimo die.
V. Anima mea turbáta est valde, sed tu, Dómine, succúrre ei.
R. Miserére mei, dum véneris in novíssimo die.
responsory5.eng:
R. Woe is me, O Lord! for I have sinned greatly in my life. I am smitten what shall I do? Whither shall I flee but unto thee, O my God?
* Have mercy upon me, when Thou comest at the latter day.
V. My soul is sore vexed, but Thou, O Lord, help me.
R. Have mercy upon me, when Thou comest at the latter day.

responsory6.label: Responsorium
responsory6.lat:
R. Ne recordéris peccáta mea, Dómine, 
* Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
V. Dírige, Dómine, Deus meus, in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
R. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
$Requiem
R. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
responsory6.eng:
R. Hold not my sins in remembrance, O Lord,
* When thou comest to judge the world by fire.
V. Make my way straight before thy face, O Lord my God.
R. When thou comest to judge the world by fire.
$Requiem
R. When thou comest to judge the world by fire.

responsory7.label: Responsorium
responsory7.lat:
R. Peccántem me cotídie, et non me pœniténtem, timor mortis contúrbat me: 
* Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
V. Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtúte tua líbera me.
R. Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
responsory7.eng:
R. Forasmuch as I sin daily, and repent not, the fear of death troubleth me.
* O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.
V. Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.
R. O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.

responsory8.label: Responsorium
responsory8.lat:
R. Dómine, secúndum actum meum noli me judicáre: nihil dignum in conspéctu tuo egi; ídeo déprecor majestátem tuam,
* Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
V. Amplius lava me, Dómine, ab injustítia mea, et a delícto meo munda me.
R. Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
responsory8.eng:
R. O Lord, judge me not according to my works; for I have done nothing that can be counted in respect of thee. I beseech thy majesty therefore, that thou wouldest
* Blot out my transgressions, O God.
V. Lord, wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.
R. Blot out my transgressions, O God.

responsory9.label: Responsorium
responsory9.lat:
R. Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda,
* Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra, * Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
V. Tremens factus sum ego et tímeo, dum discússio vénerit atque ventúra ira.
R. Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra.
V. Dies illa, dies iræ, calamitátis et misériæ, dies magna et amára valde.
R. Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
$Requiem
R. Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda, * Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra, * Dum véneris judicáre sǽculum per ignem.
responsory9.eng:
R. Deliver me, O Lord, from eternal death in that awful day;
* when the heavens and the earth shall be shaken, and Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.
V. Quaking and dread take hold upon me, when I look for the coming of the trial and the wrath to come.
R. When the heavens and the earth shall be shaken.
V. That day is a day of wrath, of wasteness and desolation, a great day and exceeding bitter.
R. When Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.
$Requiem
R. Deliver me, O Lord, from eternal death in that awful day, when the heavens and the earth shall be shaken, and Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.

Now thou art portal of the skies.
Thou art the door of heaven's high King,
Light's gateway fair and glistering;

Ye ransomed nations, praise the Lord!
All honour, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born, to thee;

hymnus_laudes.lat:
O gloriósa vírginum,
Sublímis inter sídera,
Qui te creávit, párvulum
Lacténte nutris úbere.
Quod Heva tristis ábstulit,
Tu reddis almo gérmine:
Intrent ut astra flébiles,
Cæli reclúdis cárdines.
Tu Regis alti jánua
Et aula lucis fúlgida:
Vitam datam per Vírginem,
Gentes redémptæ, pláudite.
* Jesu tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

ant_laudes.eng: O Blessed Mary, * Mother of God, Virgin for ever, temple of the Lord, sanctuary of the Holy Ghost, thou, without any example before thee, didst make thyself well-pleasing in the sight of our Lord Jesus Christ; pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God.
ant_laudes.lat: Beáta Dei Génetrix, María, * Virgo perpétua, templum Dómini, sacrárium Spíritus Sancti, sola sine exémplo placuísti Dómino nostro Jesu Christo: ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu.

oratio.lat: Concéde nos fámulos tuos, quǽsumus, Dómine Deus, perpétua mentis et córporis sanitáte gaudére: et, gloriósa beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis intercessióne, a præsénti liberári tristítia, et ætérna pérfrui lætítia.
oratio.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord God, unto all thy servants, that they may remain continually in the enjoyment of soundness both of mind and body, and by the glorious intercession of the Blessed Mary, always a Virgin, may be delivered from present sadness, and enter into the joy of thine eternal gladness.

ant_laudes.lat: Mirábile mystérium * declarátur hódie: innovántur natúræ, Deus homo factus est: id quod fuit permánsit, et quod non erat assúmpsit; non commixtiónem passus, neque divisiónem.
ant_laudes.eng: This day is set forth a wonderful mystery, * a new thing hath been created in the earth: God is made man. That which He was, He remaineth; and that which He was not, He taketh; suffering therein neither confusion nor division.

oratio.lat:
Deus, qui salútis ætérnæ, beátæ Maríæ virginitáte fecúnda, humáno géneri prǽmia præstitísti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ipsam pro nobis intercédere sentiámus, per quam merúimus auctórem vitæ suscípere, Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:
Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
oratio.eng:
O God, Who, by the fruitful virginity of the Blessed Mary, hast given unto mankind the rewards of everlasting life; grant, we beseech thee, that we may continually feel the might of her intercession, through whom we have worthily received the Author of our life, our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son:
Who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.
